findings.title: Insurance FAQ omits the BMI eligibility rule, may overstate which operations are covered, and names the former regulator
findings.where: /home/user/dralhazmi.com/src/pages/[lang]/index.astro line 137 (homepage FAQ 'Does health insurance cover weight-loss surgery?')
findings.evidence: Site: 'Under the basic health insurance policy set by Saudi Arabia's Council of Health Insurance (essential benefit package effective October 2022), approved bariatric operations are covered up to SAR 15,000 per policy period, with a copayment of 0-20% capped at SAR 1,000.' The cited PDF confirms the numbers ('Up to a maximum of 15,000 Saudi riyals during the policy period / With a copayment from 0-20% with a maximum out of pocket 1000 Saudi Riyals') but conditions it on 'if BMI exceeds 40 or 35 with complications'. The site never states this, while the same page tells readers guidelines recommend surgery from BMI 35 and consider it from 30. The Insurance Authority FAQ (ia.gov.sa/ar/faqs, last modified 09/09/2026) says the basic policy covers obesity surgery 'عن طريق عمليات تكميم المعدة (Sleeve) فقط عند تجاوز كتلة الجسم 40 أو 35 مع وجود مضاعفات' (sleeve only). The same FAQ states that since 4/3/2024 all health-insurance powers moved from the Council of Health Insurance to the Insurance Authority, so 'set by the Council of Health Insurance' describes the 2022 issuer, not the current regulator. The PDF also says the policy is updated every 3 years, so 'effective October 2022' is due for re-checking.
findings.fix: Owner to approve a corrected answer, e.g.: 'Under Saudi Arabia's basic health insurance policy (benefit package effective October 2022, now supervised by the Insurance Authority), obesity surgery is covered when BMI is above 40, or above 35 with complications, up to SAR 15,000 per policy period, with a copayment of 0-20% capped at SAR 1,000. The regulator's current guidance refers to sleeve gastrectomy; confirm the operation and criteria with your insurer before surgery.' Add the Insurance Authority FAQ as a second source and re-verify at each content review.

findings.title: Ramadan FAQ generalises the Delphi consensus beyond what it says
findings.where: /home/user/dralhazmi.com/src/pages/[lang]/index.astro line 131 (homepage FAQ 'Can I fast in Ramadan after weight-loss surgery?')
findings.evidence: Site: 'an international expert consensus advises delaying fasting for about 6 to 12 months after surgery'. According to PubMed, the abstract of the cited paper (Kermansaravi et al., Obes Surg 2021;31(12):5303-5311, https://doi.org/10.1007/s11695-021-05724-z) says: 'Seventy percent of the experts recommended delaying fasting after MBS for 6 to 12 months after combined and malabsorptive procedures according to the patient's situation and surgeon's experience'. The recommendation is limited to combined/malabsorptive procedures (e.g. bypass), not all surgery (sleeve is not covered by that statement), and 70.0% is exactly the paper's minimum threshold for consensus. The rest checks out: '96.7% advised stopping fasting in the presence of persistent symptoms of intolerance'; the NHS leaflet says 'not to fast during the first 12-18 months'; citation volume/pages are correct.
findings.fix: Owner to approve the added qualifier: 'an international expert consensus advises delaying fasting for about 6 to 12 months after bypass-type (combined or malabsorptive) operations'. Dr. Alhazmi's own recommendation sentence can stay as written.

findings.title: Present-tense academic appointment and titles need verification after leaving KFSHRC
findings.where: /home/user/dralhazmi.com/src/pages/[lang]/about.astro line 25; /home/user/dralhazmi.com/src/data/site.ts lines 18, 21; /home/user/dralhazmi.com/src/layouts/Base.astro line 26
findings.evidence: about.astro:25 'He is a Clinical Assistant Professor at Alfaisal University College of Medicine' is the only current institutional affiliation on the site and is in the present tense; such clinical appointments are commonly tied to a hospital post, and he has left KFSHRC. Separately, the public title is 'Bariatric, Metabolic & Robotic Surgeon' (site.ts:18) and 'Robotic & Bariatric Surgery' (Base.astro:26), while the licence classification the site itself lists is 'Saudi Commission for Health Specialties: Consultant, General Surgery & Bariatric Surgery' (about.astro:34). Saudi health-advertising rules expect advertised specialties to match the SCFHS classification; 'Robotic Surgeon' and 'Obesity Medicine' are certifications/training, not SCFHS specialties. I could not verify either point from the repo.
findings.fix: Owner to confirm the Alfaisal appointment is still active; if not, change to past tense ('He served as...'). Consider leading the title with the licensed classification (e.g. 'Consultant, General & Bariatric Surgery') and presenting robotic surgery and obesity medicine as training/certification beneath it. Also confirm ABS and ABOM certificates are current, since the site says 'is certified' (index.astro:109, about.astro:31-32).

findings.title: GLP-1 comparison is accurate to the press release but presented without its key limitation
findings.where: /home/user/dralhazmi.com/src/pages/[lang]/index.astro line 125 (homepage FAQ 'Are weight-loss medications an alternative to surgery?')
findings.evidence: Site: 'patients lost about five times more weight two years after sleeve gastrectomy or gastric bypass than with these injections'. Source (ASMBS release 17 June 2025) matches: 'about five-times more weight loss... at the end of two years', but it is a retrospective conference abstract in which the drug group was 'patients who received a GLP-1 prescription for at least six months (24% total weight loss vs. 4.7%)', and the same release says 'Clinical trials show weight loss between 15% to 21% for GLP-1s' and that 'as many as 70% of patients may discontinue treatment within one year'. On a surgeon's site the unqualified 'five times' reads as a comparative-superiority claim for surgery. The second cited release (May 2026) exists and supports 'Weight often returns when the medication is stopped' only via an author quote.
findings.fix: Owner to approve one added clause: '...than with these injections, partly because many patients stopped the medication; in clinical trials the medicines produce about 15-21% weight loss.' Keep both source links.

findings.title: Hero and robotic headlines imply an outcome advantage the site never substantiates

findings.title: Three different professional taglines are in use
findings.where: /home/user/dralhazmi.com/src/data/site.ts line 18; /home/user/dralhazmi.com/src/layouts/Base.astro line 26; /home/user/dralhazmi.com/public/images/og.jpg; about.astro line 17
findings.evidence: Page title/links page: 'Bariatric, Metabolic & Robotic Surgeon'; header under the name: 'Robotic & Bariatric Surgery'; share image text: 'Robotic, Bariatric & Metabolic Surgery'; About bio: 'consultant in general, bariatric and metabolic surgery'; homepage meta: 'consultant in bariatric, metabolic, robotic and general surgery and obesity medicine'. passes: Scope: read every English string in src/data/site.ts, src/layouts/Base.astro, all src/pages/[lang]/*.astro (including hidden team.astro), 404.astro, root index.astro, public/faisal/* and the built /en/ HTML; no repository file was changed.

Rule 1: no testimonials, reviews, before/after images, 'free' offers, prices or guarantees anywhere in the English site; the only 'guaranteed' is the disclaimer 'Results vary from person to person and cannot be guaranteed'. The homepage quote is the doctor's own statement, not a patient testimonial.

Rule 2: no vendor or product names in source or built output (searched for 'da Vinci', 'Intuitive'); 'robotic' is generic throughout, including 'Robotic console surgeon training' and 'Society of Robotic Surgery'.

Rule 3 (English): no visible 'book' or 'appointment' wording; buttons read 'Contact' / 'Contact on WhatsApp' / 'Request a second opinion'; WhatsApp prefill is 'Contact request: '. Remaining 'book'/'booking' are internal variable names only. Phone and WhatsApp are +966 50 970 4040 on every page, in tel:, wa.me and JSON-LD.

Faisal AI disclosure is present in the footer of every page, the homepage FAQ, the journey FAQ, the links page and the privacy notice, and the wording is consistent (not repeated beside the hero and contact-bar call links, but always on the same page).

Rule 4: no English text asks patients to send reports; second-opinion and privacy pages say not to send them and that consent is asked first. Journey step 2 'Bring any reports' refers to an in-person consultation, not sending.

Rule 5 (KFSHRC): mentioned only twice, both past tense (index.astro:109 'practiced', about.astro:17 'spent... led... served... directed'); no address, hours, map, fees or hospital affiliation in copy or JSON-LD. og.jpg contains only name, tagline and the portrait.

Rule 6: only the one real portrait is used; no stock or generated photos, logos, awards or invented statistics. The three hero stats (15+, 2 boards, FACS) trace to credentials listed on the About page.

Source check, ASMBS FAQs of bariatric surgery (fetched): '209,116 patients... 0.16%, or approximately 1 in 600', 'More than 95% of patients will successfully lose half of their extra body weight or more', bypass 'approximately 70%' with regain of 'approximately 5%' at 2 years or more, 'return to work in one or two weeks', hair loss 'between 3 and 6 months... almost always temporary', pregnancy 'waiting 12-18 months', IUD advice, pre-operative diet 'usually 2 or 3 weeks' to 'shrink the liver... makes it safer', 'low impact for the first month', 'at least yearly lab checks' all match the site.

Source check, ASMBS Life after bariatric surgery (fetched): '64 ounces of fluid or more', '60-100 grams of protein', liquid then soft then solid foods, 'a multivitamin, Vitamin B12, Calcium, Vitamin D, and Iron' for life, walking 'within just a few hours', '30 minutes per day of moderate exercising', 'every few months for the first year' then 'yearly visits with a bariatric specialist for life' all match.

Source check, NIDDK side effects (fetched): 'Follow-up interventions, surgery, and hospitalizations are relatively common within 5 years... affecting about one-third of patients' matches; bleeding, infection, leak, clots, deficiencies, gallstones, strictures and hernias are all on the page.

Source check, ASMBS news releases June 2025 and May 2026 (fetched): both exist at the cited URLs with the stated dates; 'about five-times more weight loss... at the end of two years' and 'presented at the ASMBS 2025 Annual Scientific Meeting' match the site wording.
Source check, Chelsea and Westminster NHS leaflet (fetched): 'advised not to fast during the first 12-18 months after bariatric surgery' matches.
Source check, Council of Health Insurance PDF (retrieved): SAR 15,000 per policy period and copayment 0-20% capped at SAR 1,000 match; the link still resolves. Gaps are reported as a finding.

ASMBS/IFSO 2022 statements (BMI 35 or more recommended, 30-34.9 with metabolic disease considered, lower Asian thresholds, replaced 1991 NIH criteria) and the citation 'Surg Obes Relat Dis. 2022;18(12):1345-1356' with DOI 10.1016/j.soard.2022.08.013 are consistent with the guideline; BMI calculator tiers (35 / 30 / 25) match the advice text shown.
Dates: 'Medically reviewed... Updated November 2026' and privacy 'Effective 9 November 2026' are current as of today (13 Nov 2026); footer year is generated at build time.

Privacy promise of no third-party requests holds in the built /en/ pages: no external scripts, stylesheets, fonts or images, only outbound hyperlinks. Emergency number 997 is consistent in the footer and on the second-opinion page.

Not verified (no source available in the sandbox): the doctor's personal credentials, dates, memberships and social handles; these were checked for internal consistency only. Tavily and Firecrawl were out of quota, so sources were fetched with Exa and PubMed.

findings.evidence: «خبرة تتجاوز خمسة عشر عامًا في جراحة السمنة والجراحة الأيضية والجراحة العامة، وأجرى في السنوات الأخيرة عملياته كلها تقريبًا بالروبوت.» The first clause is a noun fragment («خبرة…»), so «وأجرى… عملياته» has no antecedent; nothing on screen above it names the doctor as subject.

passes: Read every Arabic string against its English pair in src/data/site.ts, src/layouts/Base.astro, src/pages/404.astro, src/pages/index.astro and all src/pages/[lang]/*.astro (index, about, journey, second-opinion, media, links, privacy, resources, treatments/index, treatments/[slug]). team.astro (hidden) and public/faisal (English-only, noindex) were not audited.

All numbers match between languages: 15 years, BMI 35/30, 209,116 patients, 0.16% / 1 in 600, one-third within 5 years, 95%, 70%, 5% after 2 years, five times, 1.9 L (ounces sensibly dropped), 60-100 g protein, 2-3 weeks, 1-2 weeks, 30 minutes, 3-6 months, 12-18 months, 6-12 months, SAR 15,000 / 0-20% / SAR 1,000, October 2022, dates 2003-2022, 997.

Privacy notice parity is otherwise faithful: optional vs required data, 'rely on your consent' («بناءً على موافقتك»), 'explicit consent' («موافقتك الصريحة»), no sale/advertising, disclosure only if law requires, processing outside Saudi Arabia, retention and earlier deletion on request, all four rights, SDAIA complaint route, effective date.
Rule 4 parity: Arabic asks for a question only and tells users not to send reports («يُرجى عدم إرسال تقارير أو صور طبية…») exactly as English does; consent-first wording preserved.

Past-tense handling of KFSHRC and of robotic practice is preserved in Arabic («عمل استشاريًا…», «أجرى في السنوات الأخيرة عملياته كلها تقريبًا بالروبوت»); no vendor names; no superlatives or guarantees about the doctor introduced in Arabic; «ولا يمكن ضمانها» kept.

Pregnancy FAQ correctly switches to feminine address («خطّطي», «تحدّثي»); «رأي طبي ثانٍ» / «رأيًا طبيًا ثانيًا» case endings correct; tanwin placement (ًا) consistent; Arabic comma, semicolon, question mark and «» guillemets used correctly; no Latin punctuation found inside Arabic sentences.
Digits: Western digits used consistently (acceptable for a Saudi site); BMI inputs accept Arabic-Indic digits and the Arabic decimal separator.

Bidi verified by DOM geometry and my own renders in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-dralhazmi-com/303fe75a-ef20-5ba6-9a6e-8876fccac785/scratchpad/arparity/: phone numbers render '+966 50 970 4040' in correct order everywhere (bdi dir=ltr or LRM), sentence period falls on the correct side; percentages render with the sign on the left consistently (Arabic convention); year ranges read 2009 then 2010 right-to-left; 'ASMBS/IFSO', 'FACS', 'IP', 'PDF', 'ب12' sit correctly; the Kermansaravi citation and the Eisenberg source line are LTR-isolated and wrap cleanly; directional arrows (←, ↖) point the correct way for RTL.

Baseline screenshots ar-desktop-seg01/02 and ar-mobile-seg01 show correct RTL mirroring of header, hero, stats and quote; credentials line 'MD, FACS, ABS, ABOM, MBA' renders in correct order and right-aligned.

Official Arabic names checked and fine: «مجلس الضمان الصحي», «الهيئة السعودية للتخصصات الصحية», «الهيئة السعودية للبيانات والذكاء الاصطناعي (سدايا)», «نظام حماية البيانات الشخصية», «مستشفى الملك فيصل التخصصي ومركز الأبحاث», «الجمعية السعودية لطب وجراحة السمنة».

findings.fix: Add lang='en' wherever dir='ltr' wraps English prose or abbreviations (citations, credentials string, journal names). Proper names of social networks can stay as is.

findings.title: Scroll-reveal animation is dead code in the built CSS (minifier folded animation-timeline into the shorthand)
findings.where: src/styles/global.css:311-313 (.reveal); built file _astro/global.*.css
findings.evidence: Built rule is '.reveal{animation:linear both rise view();animation-range:entry cover 22%}'. In Chromium 153 with prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, CSS.supports('animation-timeline: view()') is true but getComputedStyle('.reveal').animationName is 'none' and animationTimeline 'auto' for all 23 .reveal elements; opacity stays 1 while scrolling. So the only motion on the site is the hero .intro rise. (Good side effect: no content is ever invisible to keyboard users; all 45 focus stops had opacity 1.)
findings.fix: If scroll reveals are wanted in the redesign, write animation-timeline as a separate longhand after the animation shorthand and verify in the built CSS (or exclude it from minifier merging); keep it inside the no-preference media query and make sure focused elements are never at opacity 0 (e.g. .reveal:focus-within { animation: none }).

findings.title: prefers-reduced-motion still moves buttons on hover
findings.where: global.css:125 .btn:hover { transform: translateY(-1px) } and :189-190 .t-row:hover .t-arrow translateX(6px); reduce rule at :315-317 only removes transitions
findings.evidence: With reducedMotion:'reduce' emulated, hovering '.hero .btn' gives computed transform matrix(1,0,0,1,0,-1); transitions are 0s so the button and the treatment-row arrow jump instantly instead of not moving. Entrance animations are correctly disabled (animation-name none, opacity 1).
findings.fix: Inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) also set .btn:hover, .t-row:hover .t-arrow { transform: none }, or scope the hover transforms to the no-preference query.

findings.title: Current-page indicator and link underlines disappear in forced-colors mode
findings.where: .ulink (global.css:84-91) draws its underline with background-image; nav a[aria-current='page']
findings.evidence: With forcedColors:'active' the computed background-image of .nav a[aria-current] is 'none', so the 1px underline that marks the current page (and the hover underline on every .ulink) is gone; nav items are distinguishable only as LinkText colour. Everything else survives (buttons get 1px borders, text is white on black); see /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-dralhazmi-com/303fe75a-ef20-5ba6-9a6e-8876fccac785/scratchpad/a11y/shots/fc-en-1440-top.png.
findings.fix: Add @media (forced-colors: active) { .ulink[aria-current='page'], .ulink:hover { text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: .3em } } or draw the indicator with border-bottom/text-decoration in all modes.

findings.title: No authored focus style: every link, button and summary relies on the browser default ring
findings.where: global.css (only .bmi input:focus at line 248 and main:focus are defined)
findings.evidence: Computed outline on all 43-45 tab stops per page is the UA default 'auto 1px rgb(16,16,16)'; only #bmi-h/#bmi-w get 'solid 2px rgb(14,106,112) offset 2px'. In Chromium the default two-tone ring is visible on both light and dark (.cta-band) surfaces (verified by screenshot), but it is inconsistent with the one custom ring, hugs pill buttons with a square ring, and its appearance in Safari/Firefox is not controlled by the design.
findings.fix: Add one site-wide rule, e.g. :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: inherit } with .section-dark :focus-visible, .cta-band :focus-visible { outline-color: var(--accent-light) } (#9fd3d6 on #14202b is about 10:1).

findings.title: Small touch targets for standalone text links (pass 2.5.8 only through spacing)
findings.where: .footer a.ulink (Base.astro:91-98), a.lang (Base.astro:66), FAQ source links (details p.small a), 'Your journey in detail' / 'Read the full story' links on the homepage
findings.evidence: Measured getBoundingClientRect heights: footer links 'Trusted resources', 'All links', 'Privacy' and footer phone = 17px tall in EN (22px AR); FAQ source links 17px; 'Your journey in detail →' 20px; hero-phone link on /en/links/ 20px; language switch 36x25px (EN page) / 49x28px (AR page) and it is the only way to change language on mobile; AR nav item 'نبذة' is 23.4px wide. Centres are about 30px apart so the 24px spacing exception is met, but they are far below a comfortable 44px touch size on the pages most used on phones.
findings.fix: Give standalone links block padding (padding-block: .6rem; display: inline-block; min-height: 44px on touch), make footer links a list with 44px rows on mobile, and enlarge the language switch to a 44px-high pill.

findings.title: Decorative '+' on FAQ summaries is exposed as text; step numerals are very low contrast
findings.where: global.css:225 summary::after { content: '+' }; global.css:205-208 .steps li::before colour #c9bfae
findings.evidence: getComputedStyle(summary,'::after').content is "+" with no alternative text, so screen readers that read generated content append 'plus' to all 15 homepage FAQ questions (and it does not change name when open, only rotates). .steps li::before on /en/journey/ and /en/second-opinion/ renders the step number at 35.2px in rgb(201,191,174) on #fbfaf7, about 1.75:1 (below the 3:1 large-text minimum; order is still conveyed by the <ol>).
findings.fix: Use content: '+' / '' (empty alt text) or an aria-hidden inline SVG chevron for the marker; darken the step numerals to at least 3:1 (e.g. #8a7f6c on #fbfaf7) or treat them explicitly as decoration with a real visible number elsewhere.

findings.title: Header Contact button and bottom contact bar are both shown between 641 and 819px; heading level skipped on Learn page; /faisal/ pages have no landmarks
findings.where: global.css:295-303 (breakpoints 820px vs 640px); src/pages/[lang]/media.astro (h1 then h3); public/faisal/index.html
findings.evidence: At 768px: .header .btn display:flex and .contact-bar display:flex (66.5px tall) at the same time, so the same WhatsApp action appears twice in the tab order (45 tab stops vs 43 at 1440). axe best-practice 'heading-order' on /en/media/ and /ar/media/: 'article:nth-child(1) > h3' follows the h1 directly. /faisal/: axe 'landmark-one-main' and 'region' (h1 and 4 paragraphs outside any landmark).
findings.fix: Use one breakpoint for both rules (hide the header button whenever the bar is visible, or vice versa); change the media cards to h2; wrap the /faisal/ page bodies in <main>.

passes: axe-core (wcag2a/aa, 2.1, 2.2 tags) on 18 pages at 1440, 768, 375 and 320px: 0 WCAG-tagged violations; only best-practice hits (region, heading-order, landmark-one-main) reported above
No horizontal page overflow (documentElement.scrollWidth - clientWidth = 0) on all 18 pages at 1440/768/375/320 and with WCAG 1.4.12 text-spacing overrides

Text colour contrast: every visible text node on 21 pages (FAQ details forced open) computed against its composited background, none below 5:1, including text in .section-dark and .cta-band; hover states calculated (white on #0e6a70 = 6.3:1, accent-dark and accent on #fbfaf7 above 6:1)
Skip link: first tab stop, visible when focused (ink pill, 16px from inline-start in both LTR and RTL), Enter moves focus to main#main, next Tab continues after the header
Tab order is logical and matches visual order on all 11 pages walked at 3 widths; every stop matches :focus-visible and shows a ring; focus ring is visible on dark sections in Chromium
FAQ <details>: summary is focusable, Enter opens and Space closes (verified), targets are 42px+ tall
Language switch keeps the current path (/en/about/ <-> /ar/about/) and carries lang and hreflang of the target language

BMI inputs: programmatically labelled by wrapping <label>, inputmode=decimal, 20px font (no iOS zoom), 48px min-height, custom 2px focus outline; ASCII digits, Arabic-Indic digits, Arabic decimal separator, comma decimal and trailing units all compute correctly (170/95 -> 32.9); result container has aria-live=polite; value is LTR-isolated in Arabic

RTL: arrows mirrored (-> becomes <-, external arrow becomes up-left), decorative arrows aria-hidden, .ulink underline origin, .steps padding, .portrait frame offset, .notice border and contact-bar order all mirror correctly; no Arabic text with letter-spacing, italics, text-transform or line-height below 1.3; phone numbers isolated with bdi dir=ltr
prefers-reduced-motion: entrance animations disabled (animation-name none, opacity 1), all transitions 0s, scroll-behavior auto
Forced-colors mode: text, buttons (1px borders), header, BMI card, CTA band and contact bar all remain legible at 1440 and 375 in EN and AR
Fixed contact bar does not cover the end of the page: body padding-bottom 72px vs bar 66.5/69.5px, last footer line ends 57-60px above the bar at 375, 320 and 768
Target size WCAG 2.5.8: no interactive element fails once the spacing exception is applied; buttons are 40-48px tall, contact-bar buttons 46-49px
No link has an arrow-only or empty accessible name; no two links share a name with different destinations on the pages checked; t-row links include number, title and description
Heading structure: one h1 per page, no skipped levels except /media/ (reported); page titles are unique and language-appropriate
Root / without JavaScript shows plain English and Arabic links (Arabic one has lang=ar); 404 page marks its Arabic block with lang=ar dir=rtl
Print media: contact bar hidden, no content left at opacity 0

findings.title: Hero: portrait's offset outline frame collides with the stats strip and the 'FACS' figure
findings.where: baseline/en-desktop-seg01.png (bottom right, y≈745-775) and ar-desktop-seg01.png (bottom left); global.css .portrait::before (inset 28px -28px -28px 28px) + .stats border
findings.evidence: The 1px beige outline behind the arch drops 28px below the photo, crosses the stats strip's top rule and its bottom edge sits about 5px above the cap-height of 'FACS' (zoomed crop: rule, then frame corner, then 'FACS' touching it). On mobile (en-mobile-seg02.png, ar-mobile-seg02.png) the same frame bottom sits directly on top of '15+' with no gap and the stats strip's top rule is hidden behind the photo. It reads as a layout accident on the first screen.
findings.fix: Give the hero a real bottom margin for the decoration: add padding-bottom >= 56px to .hero-grid (or margin-bottom on .portrait equal to offset + 24px), and move the stats strip out of the hero's flow into its own band with 48-64px of air above it. Alternatively drop the offset keyline and replace it with a contained device (soft sand arch panel behind the photo that ends exactly at the photo's baseline).

findings.title: Mobile hero: the only photo is entirely below the fold; first screen is text plus a sliver of hair
findings.where: baseline/en-mobile-seg01.png, ar-mobile-seg01.png; .hero-grid single column, .portrait max-width 320px
findings.evidence: At 390x844 the portrait starts at y=667 (measured) and only the top of the head is visible above the sticky contact bar. The mobile hero is 1331px tall (1.6 screens). The trust-building face, the single real image the site owns, is not seen on arrival, and the 320px arch then fills a whole screen on its own (en-mobile-seg02.png).
findings.fix: On <900px restructure the hero: a compact portrait (about 120-140px arch or circle) beside or above the eyebrow, or a 2-column mini layout (photo 38% / headline 62%), so face + headline + WhatsApp button all fit in the first 700px. Reduce hero top padding to about 2rem on phones and fold the three stats into a single 3-column row of small figures directly under the CTA.

findings.title: Persistent chrome eats about 21% of the phone viewport; nav is a clipped, unsignalled horizontal scroller
findings.where: baseline/en-mobile-seg01.png … seg10 (every mobile slice); .header (two rows, measured 109px) + .contact-bar (about 66px); .nav overflow-x:auto, scrollbar-width:none
findings.evidence: Sticky header 109px + fixed contact bar 66px = 175px of 844px always covered. Nav scrollWidth 594px in a 390px box: 'Second Opinion' and 'Learn' are invisible, with only a 2px sliver at the right edge hinting at more (en-mobile-seg01.png shows 'Your Journey' then a cut edge). In Arabic 'رأي طبي ثانٍ' is cut mid-word at the left edge (ar-mobile-seg01.png) and 'تثقيف' is hidden.
findings.fix: On phones collapse the header to a single 56px row (monogram + name, language switch, menu button) with the six links in a native <details>/popover sheet or a full-width 2x3 grid menu; or keep the scroller but add an edge fade mask plus scroll-snap and make the header hide on scroll-down / show on scroll-up (CSS scroll-driven, no JS needed, with a reduced-motion fallback). Keep the contact bar but shrink it to 56px with safe-area inset padding.

findings.title: Inner treatment and second-opinion pages are under-designed: H2s jammed against the preceding paragraph, no structure, no visual identity
findings.where: baseline/en_treatments_robotic-surgery-desktop-seg01.png, -seg02.png, en_second-opinion-desktop-seg01.png, en_treatments_robotic-surgery-mobile-seg01.png; global.css h1,h2 {margin:0 0 .6em}
findings.evidence: Headings have zero top margin, so 'What it is' sits about 28px under the lead paragraph but 45px above its own text, and 'Who it may suit' sits 20px under the previous paragraph: the heading visually belongs to the wrong block (inverted proximity). 51px serif H2s introduce one- or two-sentence paragraphs, so the page is mostly headline. The whole robotic-surgery page is 3 short paragraphs in a 772px column with about 330px of empty margin either side on a 1440 screen; no eyebrow, breadcrumb, sibling navigation, illustration or sand/dark band, whereas the homepage uses all of these.
findings.fix: Create a proper article template: page header band (sand background, eyebrow 'Treatments / 01', H1, lead, thin rule) then a 2-column layout at >=1000px: sticky left rail (on-this-page links + compact WhatsApp contact card with the Faisal disclosure) and a 62-68ch text column. Set inner-page h2 to a smaller step (clamp(1.5rem,2.4vw,2rem)) with margin-top 2.5em / margin-bottom .5em, optionally with a hairline and small numeral. End each treatment page with a prev/next treatment pager and the dark CTA band reused from the homepage.

findings.title: No illustration or iconography anywhere: nine homepage sections are text + hairlines only
findings.where: baseline/en-desktop-seg02.png through seg08.png; ar-desktop-seg02 … seg08
findings.evidence: After the hero portrait there is not a single image, icon, diagram or decorative shape for about 6500px of scroll (desktop page is 7387px tall). The 'robotic' dark section (en-desktop-seg02/03) describes '3D view', 'wristed instruments', 'small incisions' purely in 15px text; the journey (en-desktop-seg05.png) is four text columns with no connecting line. The site reads like a well-typeset document, not a 'stunning' site.
findings.fix: Add a small bespoke line-art system (inline SVG, 1.25px stroke, currentColor, about 1-2 KB each, no vendor likeness): four abstract glyphs for the robotic points (concentric lens / articulated wrist joint / three small port dots / check-ring), five for treatments, a continuous horizontal path joining the 4 journey steps (vertical on mobile). Add one large abstract motif to the dark section (e.g. fine concentric arcs echoing the portrait arch, 6-8% opacity) and reuse the arch shape as a recurring brand device (CTA band corner, page-header bands). Mirror directional glyphs in RTL.

findings.title: Monotony: the same 'rule + small numeral + title + 15px grey text' pattern is used for five consecutive sections
findings.where: baseline/en-desktop-seg02.png (.points 01-04), seg03.png (Without/With surgery .points), seg04.png (.t-list 01-05), seg05.png (journey 1-4), seg06.png (.dl), seg07.png (.faq); also en_about-desktop-seg02.png, en_resources-desktop-seg02/03.png
findings.evidence: Every component is a 1px top rule in ink with beige row dividers; .points, .t-list, .facts, .steps, .dl, .faq and .link-list in global.css are all the same pattern. Sections alternate only between #fbfaf7 and #f3f0ea (a 3% luminance difference, barely perceptible in en-desktop-seg04/05). There is one dark section and it is the second thing on the page, so the lower 70% of the page has no contrast event until the CTA.
findings.fix: Give each section its own layout idea: robotic = dark band with icon cards on a 2x2 grid beside a large motif; two paths = two real side-by-side panels (outlined card vs filled teal-tint card) with check glyphs; treatments = large interactive index (keep) but with hover reveal of a glyph and teal number; journey = connected timeline; about = portrait-led editorial split; FAQ = grouped accordion. Increase the surface range: add a pale teal tint (about #e8f1f0) and a deeper sand, and place a second dark or teal moment mid-page (e.g. the BMI checker).

findings.title: FAQ: 15 undifferentiated accordion rows with a 440px empty left column; answers and sources poorly styled
findings.where: baseline/en-desktop-seg07.png, seg08.png, en-mobile-seg10.png, ar-mobile-seg10.png; scratchpad/redesign/vd-faq-d.png and vd-faq-m.png (item 3 opened); global.css .faq / details / summary
findings.evidence: The FAQ section is 1908px tall on desktop and 2353px on mobile, closed. En-desktop-seg07.png is a full viewport of identical rows with the left 456px completely blank because the 'Common questions' H2 is not sticky and has scrolled away. No grouping, numbering or search across 15 questions about very different topics (risks, diet, pregnancy, Ramadan, who answers the phone). Opened state: answer is grey #3e4954 17px at about 95 characters per line on desktop (704px), sources are two stacked full-size underlined teal links each prefixed 'Source:' with no visual container; the open indicator is a rotated '+' glyph (text character, about 12px visual) and the summary has no hover or open-state highlight; details has no open animation.
findings.fix: Group into 4 labelled clusters (Before deciding / Risks & results / Life after surgery / Practicalities) with small eyebrow sub-heads; make the left column position:sticky (top: header height) containing the H2, a one-line intro, cluster jump links and the 'Medically reviewed' line. Style the open item: ink question, teal 2px inline-start border or tinted background, answer capped at 62ch in ink-ish colour, sources in a compact 'Sources' row (small caps label once, links as 13px chips with an external-arrow icon). Replace '+' with an SVG plus/minus in a 32px circle (44px hit area), animate height with interpolate-size / ::details-content where supported. On mobile reduce row padding and use 1.05rem questions.

findings.title: Homepage journey steps look unfinished: 14px numerals glued to the titles, no rules, no connection
findings.where: baseline/en-desktop-seg05.png, ar-desktop-seg05.png, en-mobile-seg08.png
findings.evidence: The step numbers '1 2 3 4' render at about 14px serif directly on top of the bold h3 with roughly 2px gap, while the robotic section two screens above uses '01-04' with top rules and 24px padding, and the Journey page uses large 35px beige numerals (en_journey-desktop-seg01.png). Three different numeral styles for the same idea; .big-num (4rem) exists in the CSS but is not what is rendered here. The H2 above is left alone with about 480px of empty space to its right.
findings.fix: One numeral system site-wide (e.g. two-digit teal Newsreader numerals at 1.4rem inside a 44px ring). Render the four steps as a timeline: rings connected by a 1px line (horizontal on desktop, vertical on mobile), title below, text below, with the 'Your journey in detail' link moved into the section head on the right to balance the H2.

findings.title: Type scale has a hole: 77/51px display sizes drop straight to 18px h3 and 15px body copy
findings.where: global.css h1 clamp(2.6rem,6vw,4.8rem), h2 clamp(2rem,4vw,3.2rem), h3 1.15rem, .points p / .t-desc .95rem; visible in baseline/en-desktop-seg02.png, seg04.png, seg05.png
findings.evidence: Measured desktop sizes: h1 76.8px, h2 51.2px, lead 19.2px, h3 18.4px, card text 15.2px, small 14px. There is no intermediate heading step, so components pair a 51px headline with 15px grey descriptions (en-desktop-seg05.png: 'From first message to long-term follow-up.' over 15px text). Ad hoc serif sizes are scattered: .t-name 1.9rem, .card h3 1.6rem, .bmi h3 2rem, .stat-value 2.5rem/2rem, .point-num 1.4rem, .big-num 4rem, .steps numeral 2.2rem. Body card copy at 15.2px in #3e4954 is small for an audience that includes older patients.
findings.fix: Define a tokenised modular scale (e.g. --step--1 .875, 0 1.0625, 1 1.25, 2 1.5, 3 2, 4 2.75, 5 3.75, 6 4.75rem with fluid clamps) and map every component to it. Introduce a real h3 display step (serif 1.5-1.75rem) for card titles, raise card/description copy to 1rem minimum, and cap H2 at about 2.75rem inside inner pages.

findings.title: Inconsistent vertical rhythm between sections and inside components
findings.where: baseline/en-desktop-seg03.png, seg05.png, seg06.png, en_about-desktop-seg02.png, en_journey-desktop-seg02.png
findings.evidence: Section padding is 120px top and bottom, so two adjacent light sections produce 240px voids (en-desktop-seg05.png: 130px sand strip + 120px before the H2; seg06.png: 235px of empty sand under the About block). Meanwhile inside pages elements touch: on the Journey page the 'Contact on WhatsApp' button is 24px under the steps and the 'Common questions' H2 starts 20px under the button (en_journey-desktop-seg02.png); on About, 'Education and training' H2 sits 48px under the previous list while 'Certifications' has 120px above (en_about-desktop-seg02.png). The About section's right column (dl) ends 150px above the left column's end, leaving a ragged hole.
findings.fix: Introduce spacing tokens (4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64/96/128) and a 'flow' rule: section padding clamp(3.5rem,7vw,6rem); consecutive same-colour sections share a single gap; in prose, h2 margin-top 2.5-3em, button groups margin-block 2rem. Balance split layouts with align-items:stretch or by adding content (e.g. portrait in the About block).

findings.title: Portrait treatment is inconsistent and the About page wastes it
findings.where: baseline/en-desktop-seg01.png vs en_about-desktop-seg01.png and en_about-mobile-seg01.png; .portrait-frame vs .hero-photo
findings.evidence: Homepage: arch-cropped portrait with keyline. About page: the same photo as a plain 420px rectangle with 6px radius (.hero-photo), top-aligned 140px lower than the H1 and floating in the right column with no caption. The flat studio-beige photo background (#cfc6b8-ish) meets the page background with a hard edge and the photo's bottom is cut flat at mid-chest. On mobile About, the portrait does not appear in the first screen at all (en_about-mobile-seg01.png is all text). The homepage About section (en-desktop-seg06.png, en-mobile-seg09.png) has no portrait at all.
findings.fix: One portrait language everywhere: the arch frame as the brand shape, with a sand-deep backing panel and a small caption plate ('Dr. Alaa Alhazmi, MD, FACS' + specialty) overlapping the lower inline-start corner. Use it at three sizes: hero (large), About page header (medium, beside H1 and credentials, visible on first mobile screen), homepage About block and footer/CTA (small circular or mini-arch avatar). Add a subtle bottom gradient fade into the background so the flat crop edge disappears.

findings.title: About page reads as a CV dump: flat lists and a dot-separated run-on paragraph for memberships
findings.where: baseline/en_about-desktop-seg01.png, seg02.png, seg03.png
findings.evidence: Biography paragraphs are #14202b 17px at about 625px wide with no pull-outs; 'MD, FACS, ABS, ABOM, MBA' is an unexplained 20px grey line. Certifications and Education are full-width (1192px) single-line rows with about 60% of each row empty and no dates column or issuing-body emphasis (seg02.png). Memberships are one paragraph joined by middots across 1165px, about 150 characters per line (seg03.png). Section H2s at 51px dominate one-line items.
findings.fix: Rebuild as an editorial profile: header band with portrait + H1 + a row of credential chips with full names (expandable abbr); a vertical timeline for education/training with years in a fixed inline-start column (tabular numerals) and institution in serif; certifications as a 2-3 column grid of bordered tiles (issuer name in small caps, credential in serif); memberships as a wrapped list of pill tags or a 2-column list. Past roles at the former hospital shown as a dated 'Previous experience' timeline entry to keep the past tense unambiguous.

findings.title: Line lengths exceed comfortable measure in several places
findings.where: baseline/en_about-desktop-seg03.png (Memberships), en_treatments_robotic-surgery-desktop-seg01.png, vd-faq-d.png; .narrow 820px, details p max-width 44rem
findings.evidence: Memberships paragraph about 150 characters per line; treatment body copy about 95-100 characters per line in the 772px column ('In robotic surgery, the surgeon controls precise instruments and a magnified 3D camera' is one line); FAQ answers about 95 characters per line. Comfortable reading measure is 60-75.
findings.fix: Set prose containers to max-width 65ch (about 38rem at 17px) for Latin and about 60ch for Arabic; apply to .narrow prose, details p and the About paragraphs; use text-wrap: pretty on paragraphs and text-wrap: balance on headings (the H2 'From first message to long-term / follow-up.' in en-desktop-seg05.png orphans one word).

findings.title: Arabic headings: Amiri at weight 400 is too light and calligraphic against Plex body and against the Latin scale; hero headline lacks mass
findings.where: baseline/ar-desktop-seg01.png, seg02.png, seg03.png, seg04.png, ar-mobile-seg01.png, ar-mobile-seg04.png; global.css :lang(ar) --serif 'Amiri', h1/h2 font-weight 400
findings.evidence: Arabic h1 is the same 76.8px as Latin but Amiri's small body and thin strokes make 'جراحة / بدقّة الروبوت.' occupy about 350px of a 627px column, leaving the left 45% of the headline block empty, while the Latin hero fills its column. The brand name in the header is Amiri 700 but all H1/H2 are 400, so the tiny logo looks heavier than the page headline. Amiri's wide inter-word gaps are visible in 'ليس  كل  مريض' (ar-desktop-seg03.png) and the quote (seg02.png). Amiri is a book naskh; set beside geometric IBM Plex Sans Arabic it gives a classical/religious-text tone rather than a contemporary medical one. Line-height 1.35 at 77px puts the shadda of 'بدقّة' close to the line above.
findings.fix: Either (a) keep Amiri but use weight 700 for h1/h2, scale Arabic display sizes up about 12-15% (h1 clamp(3rem,7vw,5.5rem)), tighten word-spacing (-0.05em) and set line-height 1.45; or (b, preferred) switch Arabic display to a contemporary self-hosted naskh/kufi-leaning face with real weights (e.g. Noto Naskh Arabic 600, Readex Pro, or IBM Plex Sans Arabic 600/700 for headings with Amiri reserved for the quote only), subset to keep the Arabic page under its current 470 KB. Re-balance the Arabic hero so the headline breaks into two fuller lines.

findings.title: Arabic small text is too small and loses hierarchy cues that English gets from uppercase tracking
findings.where: baseline/ar-desktop-seg01.png (stat labels), seg04.png (.t-desc), seg05.png (step text), seg06.png (dl labels), seg09.png (footer)
findings.evidence: Arabic body is bumped to 18px but components keep fixed rem sizes: .stat-label 14px, .t-desc and .points p 15.2px, footer 14.4px; Arabic at these sizes with 1.85 line-height looks sparse and faint (ar-desktop-seg04.png descriptions; seg09 footer). Eyebrows and dl labels in Arabic are plain teal/grey 15-16px text with no tracking, weight or device, so they read as body text ('مساران للعلاج' in seg03.png; 'الزمالة', 'الشهادات' in seg06.png).
findings.fix: Add an Arabic size bump for all sub-body text (min 1rem for descriptions, .9375rem for captions) and set Arabic line-height 1.7 for small text. Give Arabic eyebrows a non-typographic cue: weight 600 plus a 24px teal rule or small diamond/dot before the text (inline-start), and dl labels weight 500 in ink at .95rem.

findings.title: Latin 'AH' monogram and Latin credential string are used unchanged in the Arabic UI

The About block shows letter-spaced Latin 'MD, FACS, ABS, ABOM, MBA' under the Arabic H2 and in the footer, with no Arabic equivalent, making Arabic feel like a skin over the English design.

Keep the Latin post-nominals (they are real credentials) but set them as secondary, with an Arabic descriptor line first, and use dir=ltr isolation with normal tracking.

findings.title: Treatment/resource rows on mobile: misaligned inset, orphan arrow row, wrapped titles pushed off the number
findings.where: baseline/en-mobile-seg06.png, en_resources-mobile-seg02.png, ar-mobile-seg07.png; .t-row (flex-wrap, padding 2rem .75rem, .t-num width 2.5rem + 2rem gap)

Target about 120-140px per row. Make the whole row a visible tap target with an active-state tint.

findings.title: Resources page is two long identical link tables with an empty page header
findings.where: baseline/en_resources-desktop-seg01.png, seg02.png, seg03.png

Then 7 + 6+ rows in the exact treatment-index component at 1.9rem serif titles that wrap to 2-3 lines in a 380px title column ('IFSO: International Federation for the Surgery of Obesity and Metabolic Disorders', seg03.png), with descriptions adrift in the middle and an arrow 250px further right. No source logos are allowed, but there is also no language tag or organisation grouping, so scanning is slow.

Add in-page tabs/anchors 'For patients' / 'For professionals' in the header's empty right half along with the independence disclaimer in a tinted note.

findings.title: Colour: the teal accent and the WhatsApp action are almost absent; primary CTA is the same near-black as everything else
findings.where: baseline/en-desktop-seg01.png, seg03.png, seg08.png, en-mobile-seg01.png; global.css --accent #0e6a70, --wa #11803f (defined, never used), .btn-wa = ink

Every button ('Contact', 'Contact on WhatsApp', 'Discuss your result on WhatsApp', sticky 'WhatsApp') is #14202b on cream, identical to the dark section and CTA band colours, so the key conversion action never stands out; on mobile the sticky WhatsApp pill and the header are both black/cream. --wa is declared but unused. The palette is cream + navy + beige rules throughout: tasteful but indistinct from countless 'editorial serif' templates.
findings.fix: Assign roles: teal as the brand/action colour (primary buttons filled teal #0e6a70 with white text, 5.9:1; hover darker), ink for text and dark surfaces, a warm metallic-sand for numerals/keylines. Add a WhatsApp glyph (inline SVG) to WhatsApp buttons and a phone glyph to call buttons so the two channels are recognisable at a glance. Introduce a pale teal tint surface for the BMI card and notices, and a subtle radial teal glow or fine arc pattern on dark bands.

findings.title: 'Two paths' + BMI card: weak comparison and a dead-looking calculator

findings.evidence: 'Without surgery' / 'With surgery' are two plain text lists with no bullets, icons or card edges; they look like footer link columns. The BMI card has ghost placeholders '170' / '95' in grey that look like entered values, a 110px empty reserved result area ('Your result will appear here.'), underline-only inputs with small uppercase labels, and a full-width black button that is always present even before a result. On mobile the card's empty result area fills a third of the screen (en-mobile-seg05.png).
findings.fix: Make the two paths a paired component: two equal cards with a heading glyph, check-marked list items and a connecting 'or both' badge between them. Redesign the BMI tool as the page's interactive centrepiece: boxed inputs with unit suffixes inside the field, a horizontal BMI scale bar with guideline bands and a marker that animates to the result (static under reduced motion), result text beside it, the WhatsApp button appearing/enabled once a result exists; place it on a teal-tint or dark surface to break the cream run.

findings.title: Quote section is a large, undecorated void between hero and content
findings.where: baseline/en-desktop-seg02.png (top 545px), ar-desktop-seg02.png, en-mobile-seg02.png

findings.fix: Turn it into a designed pull-quote: oversized teal opening quotation glyph (or Arabic guillemet) hanging in the margin, quote set left/start-aligned on the 12-col grid spanning 8 columns, attribution with the mini portrait avatar and a thin rule; or merge it into the About block beside the portrait to remove one full-height section.

findings.title: Closing CTA band and footer are generic and thin
findings.where: baseline/en-desktop-seg09.png, ar-desktop-seg09.png, en_about-desktop-seg03.png

Bottom bar with copyright, privacy and the language switch. Add the arch/arc motif as a low-opacity background element.

findings.title: Header: two-row desktop header is tall (110px) and the nav is detached from the right-hand actions
findings.where: baseline/en-desktop-seg01.png (top 110px), ar-desktop-seg01.png; .header-row + .nav

The active state is a 1px underline only. The translucent header turns muddy grey when passing over the dark section (en-desktop-seg03.png, ar-desktop-seg03.png top band).
findings.fix: Single-row 72px header on >=1000px: brand at start, nav centred or right, language + Contact at end; shrink to 60px after scroll. Use a solid background (or higher opacity .98 with a saturation filter) to avoid the grey smear over dark bands, and a clearer active state (teal 2px underline offset 6px or weight 600).

findings.title: Stats strip is typographically uneven and one 'stat' is not a number
findings.where: baseline/en-desktop-seg01.png (bottom), en-mobile-seg02.png, ar-mobile-seg02.png

On mobile they stack vertically as three left-aligned items taking about 300px with no dividers. Lining figures in Newsreader sit on different optical sizes from the word.
findings.fix: Recast as a credential row rather than fake statistics: three or four compact items with a small line glyph each ('15+ years' / 'American Board of Surgery' / 'American Board of Obesity Medicine' / 'FACS') in a single bordered strip with vertical dividers; on mobile a 3-column mini grid or horizontally snapping chips directly under the CTA. Keep wording to the existing approved facts.

findings.title: Motion and interaction polish are minimal: no visible focus/hover system, reveal animation only in supporting browsers
findings.where: global.css lines 119-131 (.btn), 183 (.t-row:hover), 305-314 (motion); baseline slices show static states only
findings.evidence: Buttons only shift 1px and swap to teal on hover; there is no :focus-visible style defined globally (browser default ring on cream/navy), no active/pressed state, and rows change background by 4% alpha. Section reveal relies on animation-timeline: view() only, so Firefox/Safari users without support get no motion at all while hero has a one-off rise. Nothing responds to the 'robotic precision' theme.
findings.fix: Define a focus-visible ring token (2px teal + 2px offset, light variant on dark surfaces), pressed states, and arrow-slide/underline micro-interactions for rows and links. Add restrained signature motion under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference: hero keyline arc drawing in (SVG stroke-dashoffset), numerals counting is not needed; staggered fade for list rows via scroll-driven animation with a no-animation fallback that leaves content fully visible.

passes: Viewed 46 baseline slices (en/ar homepage desktop and mobile, about, robotic-surgery, journey, second-opinion, resources on desktop and mobile) plus two extra captures of an opened FAQ item saved at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-dralhazmi-com/303fe75a-ef20-5ba6-9a6e-8876fccac785/scratchpad/redesign/vd-faq-d.png and vd-faq-m.png; read all 317 lines of /home/user/dralhazmi.com/src/styles/global.css. No repo files were changed.

Overall art direction is coherent and restrained: cream/ink/teal palette, Newsreader + Inter pairing, and the roman/italic two-line headline device (en-desktop-seg01.png, seg02.png, seg08.png) are tasteful and worth keeping as the base.
Text contrast looks sound in every slice: ink and body greys on cream, on-dark grey on navy, teal eyebrows on cream; no low-contrast text spotted.
RTL mirroring is structurally correct: hero columns, treatment rows, arrows, FAQ plus signs, dl and footer all flip properly in ar-desktop-seg01…09 and ar-mobile slices; phone numbers stay LTR.
No horizontal page overflow seen in any 390px slice; only the nav strip scrolls (by design).
Treatment index on desktop (en-desktop-seg04.png) is the strongest component: clear numbering, serif names, descriptions and arrows align on a consistent grid.
Journey page numbered list (en_journey-desktop-seg01.png, en_journey-mobile-seg01.png) is clean and scannable, if plain.
Button sizes and the sticky mobile contact bar meet touch-target expectations (48px / 44px heights); WhatsApp and call are always reachable on phones.
Hero copy hierarchy on desktop (eyebrow, two-line H1, lead, CTA + phone) is clear and the English headline fills its column well.
Compliance-sensitive visuals: no testimonials, before/after imagery, vendor names, stock or generated people photos, or invented badges appear in any slice reviewed.

findings.title: Web fonts are 77-97% of page weight; Arabic pages download 399 KB of fonts (Amiri alone is 248 KB)
findings.where: src/layouts/Base.astro lines 2-11 (@fontsource imports); built files /_astro/amiri-arabic-400-normal.D0NIBXga.woff2 (108,560 B), amiri-arabic-700-normal.D8FrblyB.woff2 (99,968 B), ibm-plex-sans-arabic-arabic-400/600 (42,848 + 45,688 B)
findings.evidence: Measured at 390px, CPU 4x, 1.6 Mbps / 150 ms RTT, cold cache (3 runs, stable). /en/: 11 requests, 240.9 KB, fonts 185.7 KB in 7 files, last font at 1.83 s. /ar/: 13 requests, 455.5 KB, fonts 399.1 KB in 9 files, last font (Amiri 400, the H1 face) at 2.76 s, so Arabic headings sit in the fallback face for about 1.9 s after first paint (FCP 0.85-0.93 s). /ar/treatments/robotic-surgery/: 413 KB total, of which 399 KB is fonts and 2.1 KB is the HTML. /en/about/: 184.5 KB, fonts 136.9 KB. Amiri ships 5,429 glyphs (Quranic marks, alternates); the whole site uses 44 distinct Arabic characters. I subset the shipped files with fontTools: keeping the full U+0600-06FF block with all OpenType features gives Amiri 400 = 74.4 KB (from 108.6), Plex Arabic 400 = 28.8 KB (from 42.8), Plex 600 = 31.0 KB (from 45.7), Inter about 13.6-14.0 KB each (from about 24), Newsreader 13.0-14.4 KB each (from 22.5-24.3). Subsetting to only the glyphs the site uses gives Amiri 400 = 36.5 KB, Plex 400 = 13.4 KB, Inter about 9.6 KB, Newsreader about 11.2-12.3 KB.
findings.fix: Replace the @fontsource CSS imports with hand-written @font-face rules that point at build-time subsets (run pyftsubset or glyphhanger in a prebuild script, keep layout-features=*). Robust option (full Arabic block + ASCII + the punctuation in use): measured /en/ 240.9 -> 129.8 KB (-46%) and /ar/ 455.5 -> 239.1 KB (-48%), all fonts loaded by 0.9-1.5 s instead of 1.8-2.8 s. Aggressive option (only glyphs present in the built HTML, regenerated on every build): /en/ 111.4 KB, /ar/ 160.1 KB (-65%), fonts done by 0.8-1.2 s. Both figures include the three fixes in the next findings (Amiri 700, language-switch word, monogram). Optional extra: a variable Inter would replace three static weights with one file.

findings.title: Amiri Bold (120 KB) is downloaded on every Arabic page for the brand name only
findings.where: src/styles/global.css line 110 (:lang(ar) .brand-name { font-weight: 700 }) and line 284 (:lang(ar) .footer-name { font-weight: 700 }); /_astro/amiri-arabic-700-normal.D8FrblyB.woff2 and amiri-latin-700-normal.DIjoEGk6.woff2
findings.evidence: Above-the-fold font map on /ar/ shows the only weight-700 Amiri text is the header brand name "د. علاء الحازمي"; the footer name is the only other use. Those two rules trigger amiri-arabic-700 (99,968 B) plus amiri-latin-700 (20,300 B, fetched only for the space and full stop), which is 120.3 KB or 26% of the Arabic homepage, and they compete for bandwidth with the H1 and body faces.
findings.fix: Either set the Arabic brand and footer name to Amiri 400 (saves 120.3 KB and 2 requests per Arabic page), or keep the bold look with a 700 subset limited to the name string (measured 13.3 KB + 0.6 KB, saving about 106 KB), or render the Arabic wordmark as inline SVG paths (0 font bytes).

findings.title: English pages download a 42.8 KB Arabic font to draw one word (the language switch)
findings.where: src/layouts/Base.astro line 67 (العربية) with src/styles/global.css lines 16-22 (--sans stacks)
findings.evidence: On /en/ and /en/about/ the request log shows /_astro/ibm-plex-sans-arabic-arabic-400-normal.CyU-ddYS.woff2 (42,848 B) fetched at VeryHigh priority; the only Arabic text on those pages is "العربية" in the header. That is 23% of /en/about/ (184.5 KB) and 18% of /en/, on every English page. A subset containing only that word is 3,968 B.
findings.fix: Give the switch a system font, for example html:lang(en) .lang { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif } (iOS and Android both ship good Arabic system faces): saves 42.8 KB and 1 request per English page. If the brand face matters there, serve the 4 KB one-word subset. Do the mirror on Arabic pages: "English" plus digits currently pull the Plex latin 400 and 600 files (19.2 + 20.5 KB).

findings.title: Arabic pages download Newsreader Latin (22.5 KB) for the 'AH' monogram and numerals, plus four Latin subset files (79.5 KB) mostly for spaces, digits and punctuation
findings.where: src/styles/global.css line 106 (.monogram font-family: 'Newsreader'), lines 159/167/174/184/207/250 (numerals hard-coded to Newsreader); @fontsource unicode-range split in /_astro/global.nH6oAbt7.css
findings.evidence: /ar/ request log: newsreader-latin-400-normal (22,480 B), amiri-latin-400 (19,544), amiri-latin-700 (20,300), ibm-plex-sans-arabic-latin-400 (19,164), ibm-plex-sans-arabic-latin-600 (20,500). The fontsource Arabic subset's unicode-range excludes U+0020 (space), ASCII digits and the full stop, so any Arabic sentence triggers the matching Latin file as well. Subsets I generated: Newsreader with 'AH', digits, '+', '.' = 2,204 B; ASCII-only versions of the four Latin files = 12.7-14.7 KB each.
findings.fix: Build each Arabic face as one file covering Arabic + ASCII space, digits and punctuation, with a single unicode-range. This removes 4 requests per Arabic page and about 25-40 KB. Serve a digits + 'AH' Newsreader subset (2.2 KB, saves 20 KB) or draw the monogram as inline SVG.

findings.title: Render-blocking CSS is 64% unused @font-face rules, split over two requests, with two base64 fonts embedded
findings.where: /_astro/global.nH6oAbt7.css (26,200 B) and /_astro/Base.CARRmTtf.css (11,631 B), both linked in <head> of every page
findings.evidence: The two stylesheets are 37.8 KB raw / 11.8 KB gzip and both block rendering (they finish at 0.51 s and 0.65 s; FCP is 0.74-0.93 s). They contain 44 @font-face rules = 24.3 KB raw; Base.CARRmTtf.css is 100% @font-face. A page uses 5-9 of them; 30 are Cyrillic, Greek, Vietnamese and Latin-ext subsets no page can trigger, and every rule also lists a legacy .woff fallback. Vite inlined two IBM Plex cyrillic-ext fonts as data: URIs (2,092 + 2,126 B of base64) into the blocking CSS. The hand-written design system is only 13.5 KB raw / 3.6 KB gzip, and only two classes in it are unused in the built HTML (.draft, which is the draft banner, and .word). The HTML also uses class "hero-phone" (links.astro line 23), which has no CSS rule.
findings.fix: Ship only the 6 (English) or 9 (Arabic) faces each language needs, woff2 only, and inline the stylesheet (astro.config build.inlineStylesheets: 'always'). Measured result: 14.8 KB raw / 3.8 KB gzip of inline CSS, HTML for /ar/ becomes 12.9 KB gzip instead of 9.1 + 11.8 KB over three requests. With subsetting and inlining together, FCP fell from 0.82 -> 0.28 s on /en/, 0.85-0.93 -> 0.31 s on /ar/, and 0.67 -> 0.31-0.33 s on the Arabic treatment page; requests fell from 11 -> 8 and 13 -> 11.

findings.title: Hero intro animation starts at opacity 0 and delays LCP by about 540 ms on the Arabic homepage
findings.where: src/styles/global.css lines 305-309 (@keyframes rise from opacity:0; .intro-2 delay 0.15s; .intro-3 delay 0.3s) applied to the H1, lead paragraph and button row in src/pages/[lang]/index.astro
findings.evidence:
On /ar/ at 390px the LCP element is

(area 43,928 px, larger than the visible part of the portrait at 37,052 px). FCP is 0.85-0.93 s but LCP is 1.42-1.45 s in all three runs, because the paragraph is invisible during the 0.3 s delay plus the start of the fade. Overriding the keyframes to animate transform only (opacity untouched) gave LCP 0.87-0.91 s, equal to FCP: -540 ms. On /en/ the same effect shows on the H1 candidate (painted 348 ms after FCP), though there the portrait is the final LCP.
findings.fix: Keep the motion but do not hide content: animate transform only for .intro/.intro-2/.intro-3, or animate opacity only on decorative elements and never on the H1 and lead. Measured saving: about 540 ms LCP on /ar/ at no byte cost. prefers-reduced-motion handling is unaffected.

findings.title: Links page serves the 142 KB full-size JPEG for a 120 px avatar and it is that page's LCP
findings.where: src/pages/[lang]/links.astro line 20:
findings.evidence: /en/links/ and /ar/links/ download /images/dr-alaa-alhazmi.jpg at 142,117 B (990x977) and display it at 120x118 CSS px. It is 49% of /en/links/ (292.4 KB) and makes LCP 1.89-1.90 s on /en/links/ and 2.57-2.60 s on /ar/links/, versus FCP 0.74-0.80 s. This is the page social-media bios point to, so it is mostly opened on phones. A 240 px WebP of the same portrait is 4,006 B and a 360 px one is 7,804 B.
findings.fix: Import the portrait from src/assets and use Astro's <Image> with widths [120, 240, 360], sizes="120px", loading="eager", fetchpriority="high". Saves about 134-138 KB per view. In the font-subset test build the same page's LCP was still 1.25-1.31 s (en) and 1.48-1.76 s (ar) with the JPEG in place, so the image is the remaining bottleneck. Keep the JPEG in public/ only as the JSON-LD and Open Graph reference.

findings.title: Hero portrait srcset/sizes do not match the rendered box: image is always upscaled about 1.25x and about 21% of downloaded pixels are cropped away
findings.where: src/pages/[lang]/index.astro line 176 (<Image widths={[320,440,640,880]} sizes="(max-width: 899px) 320px, 440px">) with src/styles/global.css lines 147-148 (.portrait-frame aspect-ratio 4/5; img object-fit: cover)
findings.evidence: The source is nearly square (990x977) but the frame is 4:5 with object-fit: cover, so the image must be as tall as the box. Desktop 1440 @1x: box 440x550, browser picks the 440w file (intrinsic 440x434) and stretches it to 557x550, a 1.27x upscale. Desktop @2x: picks 880x868 for an 1114x1100 need. Mobile 390 @2x: box 314x393, picks 640x632 for a 796x786 need (1.24x). In every case about 21% of the fetched width is hidden by the crop. On 3x phones the 880w file (35,578 B) is fetched where the 640w (22,086 B) is visually equivalent for a photo. The LCP image itself is discovered early (request starts at 0.19 s, High priority, loading=eager, fetchpriority=high), so no preload is needed.
findings.fix: Crop at build time to the displayed 4:5 ratio (Astro Image width/height with fit="cover", or a pre-cropped asset) and declare true sizes, e.g. widths [320, 480, 640, 780] and sizes="(max-width: 899px) min(320px, calc(100vw - 76px)), 440px". That fixes the softness at about the same bytes. Add AVIF via <Picture formats={['avif','webp']}>: Pillow encodes of the same portrait gave 640w 15.3 KB AVIF (q55) vs 20.7 KB WebP (q80) and 880w 26.1 vs 33.8 KB (settings not quality-matched; treat as roughly 20-25% saving). about.astro line 59 is correct as is (840w for a 342-420 px box).

findings.title: Adding font preloads to the current build makes first paint slower, not faster
findings.where: src/layouts/Base.astro <head> (no preload today); applies to any redesign that adds <link rel="preload" as="font">
findings.evidence: Test build identical to live plus two font preloads per language (body + heading face): FCP went from 0.82 -> 1.07 s on /en/, 0.85-0.93 -> 1.20 s on /ar/, 0.74-0.77 -> 0.96 s on /en/about/ and 0.67 -> 0.92 s on the Arabic treatment page, because the preloaded fonts (46 KB English, 151 KB Arabic) compete with the render-blocking CSS on a 1.6 Mbps link. The only gain was Arabic CLS (0.017 -> 0.003). Even with subset fonts and inline CSS, preloading two fonts gave FCP 0.48-0.57 s versus 0.28-0.32 s without preloads, and pushed the /en/ portrait LCP from 0.83 s to 0.96-1.02 s.
findings.fix: Do not add font preloads while fonts are this large. Subset and inline the CSS first; inline CSS already lets the browser discover fonts at about 0.35 s instead of 0.67 s. If a preload is wanted afterwards, limit it to one small above-the-fold face (under about 15 KB) and re-measure.

findings.title: GitHub Pages cannot serve long-lived cache headers, so every hashed asset is revalidated after 10 minutes
findings.where: .github/workflows/deploy.yml (actions/deploy-pages) and public/CNAME; affects /_astro/* fonts, CSS and images
findings.evidence: GitHub Pages sends Cache-Control: max-age=600 for all files and offers no header configuration, so the content-hashed, immutable /_astro/ files cannot be marked immutable. I could not confirm the live headers from this sandbox (it cannot reach dralhazmi.com); this is GitHub Pages' documented default. A returning visitor after 10 minutes, or anyone navigating to a second page later, issues a conditional request for each of the 11-13 resources per page (9 of them fonts on Arabic) before the web fonts can be reused.
findings.fix: Cheapest: cut the number of files (subsetting, merged Arabic+ASCII faces and inline CSS bring pages to about 6-8 requests). Fuller fix: host on a static platform with header control (for example a _headers rule '/_astro/* Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable') or put a CDN in front of Pages. Either changes hosting, not page content, but the privacy page's description of who sees request logs should be checked against the new host before switching.

findings.title: The root URL shows nothing until a JavaScript redirect runs, adding a full extra navigation for first-time visitors
findings.where: src/pages/index.astro (inline script: location.replace(ar ? '/ar/' : '/en/'))
findings.evidence: /index.html is 1,885 B with an inline script that redirects to /en/ or /ar/. A visitor typing dralhazmi.com pays one extra document round trip (at least 150 ms RTT on the emulated link, more on a cold connection) before the real page starts loading; I did not get a reliable isolated timing for it. With JavaScript disabled the visitor only sees two plain links.
findings.fix: GitHub Pages cannot do a server redirect, so keep the script but add <link rel="prefetch" href="/en/"> and <link rel="prefetch" href="/ar/"> (about 8-9 KB gzip each) so the target document is already in cache, and add a <noscript><meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0;url=/en/"></noscript> fallback.

findings.title: Deploy ships 84 font files (1.86 MB) of which at most 16 can ever be requested
findings.where: dist/_astro/ produced from src/layouts/Base.astro and src/pages/404.astro @fontsource imports
findings.evidence: _astro/ holds 93 files / 2.06 MB: 42 legacy .woff files (1,029,376 B) that no browser supporting unicode-range will fetch, and 42 .woff2 files (831,936 B) of which only the latin and arabic subsets (16 files) match characters on the site. No visitor cost, but it bloats the Pages artifact and hides what is really served.
findings.fix: Falls out of the custom @font-face fix: emit woff2 only, for the latin/arabic subsets only. The deployed font folder drops from about 1.86 MB to about 0.2-0.3 MB.

findings.title: Small font-swap layout shifts on first load (CLS 0.006-0.019)
findings.where: font-display: swap on all 44 faces in /_astro/*.css; fallback stacks in src/styles/global.css lines 16-22
findings.evidence: CLS measured 0.018-0.019 on /en/, 0.017 on /ar/, 0.014 on /en/about/, 0.006 on the Arabic treatment page; all below the 0.1 threshold. Largest single shift is 0.0139 on /ar/ at 2.04 s, when the Arabic face arrives and the hero button row and portrait move up 35 px; on /en/about/ the whole header and main move 13 px at 1.52 s.
findings.fix: After subsetting, fonts arrive within about 0.3-0.6 s of first paint and measured CLS was 0.000-0.004 with no further work. For the remainder, add metric-matched fallback faces (@font-face with local() plus size-adjust / ascent-override) for Georgia->Newsreader and the system Arabic face->IBM Plex Sans Arabic/Amiri.

findings.title: Performance budget to hold the redesign to
findings.where: Whole site; relevant to any new hero art, motion or typography added in the redesign
findings.evidence: Today the non-font payload is already small: /en/ is 7.9 KB HTML + 11.8 KB CSS + 35.6 KB image (gzip), with one 780-byte inline module script (the BMI calculator) and zero third-party requests. Total blocking time under 4x CPU throttle is 23-195 ms from a single 82-199 ms task at first render; the homepage has 335 DOM nodes.
findings.fix: Suggested ceilings, all reachable per the measurements above: English page <= 130 KB and Arabic <= 240 KB cold (or 110 / 160 KB with per-build glyph subsetting), <= 8 requests English / <= 11 Arabic, no new font families or weights, decorative art as inline SVG or CSS gradients rather than raster images, any scroll or entry motion on transform only and never opacity:0 on the H1, lead or portrait, and JavaScript kept to the existing inline calculator.

passes: Method: Playwright Chromium, 390x844 viewport at DPR 3, CDP CPU throttle 4x and network 1.6 Mbps down / 750 kbps up / 150 ms latency, cache disabled, 3 baseline runs per page (results within about 5%). Text assets counted at gzip size, as GitHub Pages serves them. Localhost has no DNS/TLS cost, so real-world absolute times will be about 0.3-0.5 s higher; the deltas hold.

Baseline numbers: /en/ 11 requests, 240.9 KB, FCP 0.82 s, LCP 0.83 s (portrait img); /ar/ 13 requests, 455.5 KB, FCP 0.85-0.93 s, LCP 1.43-1.45 s (lead paragraph); /en/about/ 9 requests, 184.5 KB, FCP = LCP 0.74-0.77 s (first paragraph); /ar/treatments/robotic-surgery/ 12 requests, 413.0 KB, FCP = LCP 0.66-0.68 s (first paragraph).

LCP image on the English homepage is handled correctly: loading=eager, fetchpriority=high, discovered by the preload scanner at 0.19 s with High priority, finished at 0.70 s; width/height attributes present, so no image-caused layout shift. No preload is needed.
CLS is within the good threshold on all pages (0.006-0.019) and there is no horizontal overflow at 390px (scrollWidth 390 on all four pages).

JavaScript cost is negligible: one 780-byte inline module script on the homepage (BMI calculator), no external scripts, no framework runtime; inner pages have no script at all. JSON-LD is inline and small.
No third-party requests on any measured page: every request was same-origin (document, 2 CSS, fonts, at most 1 image), consistent with the privacy notice.
HTML is lean: /en/ 25.3 KB raw / 7.9 KB gzip, /ar/ 33.9 KB / 9.1 KB, inner pages 2.1-2.4 KB gzip; 335 DOM nodes on the homepage, 86-95 on inner pages.
Hand-written CSS in global.css has almost no dead code: 13.5 KB raw / 3.6 KB gzip, and only .draft (draft banner, needed) and .word are unused across all built pages.
font-display: swap is set on every face, so text is never invisible while fonts load.
Weight matching produces no synthetic bold: Arabic weight-500 text (buttons, FAQ summaries) resolves to the real Plex 400 file and bold to the real 600 file.
The about page portrait srcset is correct (420w/840w with sizes '(max-width: 460px) 100vw, 420px'; the 840w file is chosen for a 342-420 px box on 2x/3x screens).
Scroll reveal uses CSS scroll-driven animation behind @supports and prefers-reduced-motion, with no JavaScript or IntersectionObserver cost.
The two /faisal/ static pages use inline <style> only, with no external CSS, fonts, scripts or images.
og.jpg (1200x630, 52 KB) and apple-touch-icon.png (180x180, 2.3 KB) are appropriately sized and are not loaded by normal page views.

No file in /home/user/dralhazmi.com was modified. Test builds and measurement scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-dralhazmi-com/303fe75a-ef20-5ba6-9a6e-8876fccac785/scratchpad/perf (m.js, build.py, sub/ for the subset fonts, base*.json and B*.json for raw results).

exemplars.name: Mr Christopher West, consultant plastic surgeon (UK, launched Aug 2025)
exemplars.whatWorks: The closest model for a single-surgeon editorial site. Hero is a 3-word H1 plus two plain sentences, with no slogan. Trust comes from pull quotes in his own voice that show restraint ("deciding what not to operate on"). Credentials are a 4-cell fact row (FRCS (Plast), PhD, Fellowship, 80+ a year), each with a one-line plain explanation, and the post-nominals sit as one quiet line under the bio. Procedures are explained with numbered anatomical cross-section illustrations (01 Skin ... 05 Deep fascia), so illustration carries the page where photography cannot. A 4-fact operation strip (time in theatre, anaesthetic, swelling, final result) is a reusable pattern for treatment pages. Treatments are 2 featured cards plus a compact list of the rest. Do not copy: before/after pairs and Google reviews (banned here). Agency write-up: https://waywestdesign.co.uk/project/website-and-brand-direction-for-mr-christopher-west/

exemplars.name: Ms Li Jiang, consultant ophthalmic surgeon (UK, 2026, bilingual EN/Chinese)
exemplars.whatWorks: Best patient-journey and plain-language structure I read. H1 "Clearer vision, explained properly" plus one sentence promising one surgeon from first consultation to last follow-up. A hairline row of professional-body names (GMC, Royal College, ESCRS) as text, not a logo wall. A 3-step numbered journey (01 Meet / 02 Treat / 03 Live) with one honest paragraph each, including uncertainty. "Start where you are" cards let patients self-identify by situation before any procedure is named. A 4-cell credential strip (FRCOphth, Consultant-led, Five clinics, 45 min). FAQ at the bottom with numbered-step answers. Case study says the palette is deep navy, clear blue and one lime accent, with a single spiral mark reused from logo to buttons: https://aethus.co.uk/case-studies/li-jiang. Do not copy: prices, patient films, Doctify reviews.

exemplars.name: Odyssée Clinic (Awwwards Site of the Day, 8 Oct 2026, by Nightjar)
exemplars.whatWorks: Shows how far two colours can go: Awwwards lists the whole palette as deep navy #1E305E on warm off-white #F6F4F2, tagged Luxury / Clean / Minimal / Transitions / Microinteractions (https://www.awwwards.com/sites/odyssee). Short declarative headings ("Method, not myth."), parenthesised editorial numerals "(1). (2). (3). (4)." for the reasons list, and a ruled contact table with single-letter labels (A. address, C. contact). With little photography, the designer used one abstract sphere as a recurring quiet motif, described as "refined without becoming cold" (https://tympanus.net/codrops/2026/06/25/shaping-stories-into-experience-the-work-of-kevin-lam/). Its motion uses GSAP; reproduce the feel with CSS only.

exemplars.name: Neko Health (preventive health clinics)
exemplars.whatWorks: Discipline of statement. A 5-word H1 ("Your health, ahead of time"), one supporting sentence, then exactly 3 facts as a strip (One hour / Instant results / price). Each section is one idea: a short H2 plus 2-3 sentences. A three-part sequential story (A record of your body, A clear plan forward, Every visit you know more) is the model for a calm journey section. One contact line at the end instead of a form.

exemplars.name: Dr Girish Juneja, bariatric and metabolic surgeon (Dubai)
exemplars.whatWorks: Best information architecture among the bariatric sites, and it matches Dr. Alhazmi's surgery plus obesity-medicine positioning. "Where are you in your weight-loss journey?" offers 6 numbered self-identification cards (considering GLP-1, medication plateaued, weight returned, considering surgery, regain after surgery, not sure). "One condition. Several treatment tools." sets out 4 approaches as equal-weight cards. A 4-verb process (Understand, Choose, Review, Adapt). The reassurance line "You do not need to choose a procedure before meeting the doctor." Do not copy: counters that render as "0+" until JavaScript runs, and "book" wording.

exemplars.name: Dr Atef Bassas, bariatric surgeon (Riyadh and Makkah, EN/AR)
exemplars.whatWorks: Direct local peer. Good: a "Medically reviewed by ... · Last updated: October 2026" line under the hero, a numbered "Medical sources" list (ASMBS/IFSO 2022, Mayo Clinic, NIDDK) above the FAQ, a "Sleeve or bypass: which one is for me?" comparison block, and WhatsApp as the primary channel. Avoid: it asks patients to send name, age, weight and height, shows packages and instalment offers, and says "first follow-up visit free", all of which break this site's rules. Visually it is a plain text page, so the bar for a Saudi bariatric surgeon site is low.

exemplars.name: Cleveland Clinic London, Bariatric Surgery
exemplars.whatWorks: Academic-centre tone for a treatment page. Opens with empathy before credentials ("This is a big decision, and we understand that."). Then four bolded-label reasons, a "What to expect during your evaluation" block with explicit BMI criteria as a 3-item list, and each procedure as an H3 with a 3-4 sentence plain description that includes downsides (mini-bypass "can have a higher risk of complications"). The order to borrow is empathy, criteria, options, what to expect, recovery.

exemplars.name: The London Clinic (premium private hospital, WCAG AA redesign)
exemplars.whatWorks: The phone number is persistent at the very top of every page. H1 is 7 words plus one sub-line. The specialty grid uses a short title and a single sentence written around the patient's worry. "Why choose" is 4 cells, each a headline plus one sentence. The agency reports the redesign followed WCAG 2.1 AA, with a 20% rise in self-pay enquiries and conversion from 7% to 9% (https://manifesto.co.uk/client-stories/healthcare/empowering-patients-at-the-london-clinic), which is evidence that accessible and calm converts.

exemplars.name: Vanash Patel, consultant colorectal and robotic surgeon (UK)
exemplars.whatWorks: The name is the H1, with title and post-nominals directly beneath. Three plain doors follow (About / Treatments / Contact), then a first-person philosophy quote. The build notes describe treatments organised by condition as patients describe it, each publication given its own page with a plain-language summary instead of a CV link, and WhatsApp as the contact route with no form queue (https://spiritual.agency/project/vanash-patel-consultant-surgeon/). Do not copy: the long wall of patient testimonials.

exemplars.name: Dr Grigoriak, plastic surgeon, Dubai (CSS Design Awards Website of the Day; Awwwards Honorable Mention, Apr 2026)
exemplars.whatWorks: The award-winning end of surgeon personal sites, useful mainly as a contrast. Borrow: a custom line-icon set drawn only for this site, one icon per procedure; the doctor's messages in his own voice; "copy design" (type as the layout); and a content structure that rewards return visits (https://videinfra.com/work/dr-grigoriak, https://www.awwwards.com/sites/dr-grigoriak). Avoid: the near-black palette (#000000 / #201C1B), a Three.js 3D hand, "Leading Surgeon in Dubai", "2900 satisfied patients" counters and before/after galleries.
