Second opinion: the closing crop-marked block promoted to the page hero, followed by chapters; still asks for a question only. Resources/Learn: the typographic index pattern with source name, description and external arrow. Privacy: a single 65-character reading column with chapter numerals and no decoration. All pages share the header, numbered section rule, colophon footer and contact bar; the arcs drawing is limited to robotic content.
design:a-quiet-luxury.pageWeightKB: Measured by recording every file Chromium actually requested (uncompressed bytes on disk; html and css would be smaller gzipped). index.html: 279 KB at 1440px (1x), 294 KB at 390px (3x, larger portrait); with gzip on html/css about 229 / 244 KB. Breakdown: Newsreader opsz variable 132 KB, Newsreader italic 24 KB, Inter 400+500 48 KB, CSS 36 KB, HTML 32 KB, portrait 14 or 29 KB. ar.html: 286 KB at 1440px, 301 KB at 390px (about 229 / 244 KB with gzip): Markazi Text Arabic 41 KB + Latin 26 KB, Plex Arabic 400+600 89 KB, Inter 48 KB, CSS 36 KB, HTML 40 KB, portrait. treatment.html: 221 KB. Baseline for comparison is about 250 KB English and 470 KB Arabic, so Arabic drops by roughly 170 KB and English rises by roughly 30-45 KB.
design:a-quiet-luxury.selfCritique: Not verified: axe was not run, so "0 violations" is unconfirmed; contrast was calculated by hand, not measured. I did not test keyboard order, 200% zoom, 375px exactly (the helper checks 390px, no overflow reported), Firefox or Safari. The English page is heavier than the baseline because the Newsreader optical-size file alone is 132 KB; that buys the finer display cut, but the static 22 KB files would look nearly as good and save about 85 KB. The hero accent line is roman, not italic, because the italic I ship is the text cut and mismatched the display roman; the baseline's italic line had charm that this loses. Markazi Text is light and modern but reads plainer than Amiri at hero size, and its Latin numerals (15+, FACS, 01-04) look sturdier than the Newsreader figures on the English page, so the two languages are not perfectly matched; a native Arabic reader should judge the Arabic headings. The hero is still text-left, portrait-right with a three-cell strip, which is refined, not a new composition. Section labels 03 and 06 behave differently from the others (h2 as label; review dateline as label), which is a small inconsistency. The mobile nav wraps to two rows instead of a designed menu. The desktop floating WhatsApp pill can overlap content at the bottom corner (it covered the Arabic portrait caption's end in one screenshot). The 15 FAQs are not grouped by topic because that would need new headings. I added the approved Faisal note and site title in new positions (hero, closing block, portrait caption) and a few aria-labels in both languages (navigation, breadcrumb, footer), which the owner should confirm. Inner links other than index/ar/treatment are '#'. The pages are generated by a small Node script outside the deliverable folder; porting to Astro is straightforward but not done. With more time: run axe and a keyboard pass, try the static Newsreader files and Amiri-vs-Markazi side by side, design the mobile menu, and build Arabic treatment and About pages.

design:b-precision-dark.name: b-precision-dark — "Precision"
design:b-precision-dark.concept: The site is treated as a calibrated instrument: the one real portrait sits inside a ticked dial with a single luminous teal arc, and that vocabulary (tick rulers, concentric arcs, an instrument-path curve) recurs as the only decoration. Deep ink sections (hero, robotic, journey, closing call, footer) carry the cinematic moments, while warm paper and sand sections carry everything that has to be read: paths, treatments, risks, about and the FAQ. Data is set in monospace (phone number, indices, the BMI read-out on a mirrored scale) and headlines in a light serif, so the page feels exact but still warm. Arabic is composed separately, with a large Markazi Text display, IBM Plex Sans Arabic body, no tracking or italics, and a mirrored layout in which the portrait, digits and Latin credentials stay unmirrored. All approved copy, the 15 sourced FAQs, the Faisal disclosure, the 997 note and the Contact-only calls to action are reproduced verbatim from the repo.
design:b-precision-dark.typography: English: Newsreader 300 for display (h1 up to 5.5rem, tracking -0.028em) and 400 for small serif headings; Inter 400/500 for body at 17px/1.6; IBM Plex Mono 400 for eyebrows, indices, the phone number and BMI values with tabular figures. Arabic: Markazi Text variable at weight 500 for display (h1 up to 8.6rem, sized up because the face is compact); IBM Plex Sans Arabic 400/600 for body at 18px/1.85 and for labels (SemiBold, no tracking, no uppercase); Latin digits and tokens fall through to Plex Mono, Inter and Newsreader. A global :lang(ar) reset forces letter-spacing 0 and text-transform none; font-synthesis is off; emphasis is by accent colour only, never italic, in both languages. All sizes are rem + vw clamps with max at most 2.5x min. Amiri is dropped.
design:b-precision-dark.palette: Ink #06141B and raised ink #0B1F29 for dark surfaces; paper #F6F4EF and sand #ECE8DF for reading surfaces. One accent in two tunings: luminous teal #62E6D6 on dark only, and deep teal #0A6763 on paper for text and links. Text on dark is #EAF2F3 with #A9BEC3 secondary; on light it is #06141B, #2A3B43 body and #53656C muted. Hairlines are 16% and 30-40% tints of the text colour. The only filled, high-contrast element on any screen is the teal Contact / WhatsApp button. axe-core reports 0 violations on all three pages.
signatureMoves: Portrait dial: the single photo in a circular mask inside an SVG ring of 180 calibrated ticks, crosshair stubs and one teal arc that draws once on load; the credentials (MD · FACS · ABS · ABOM · MBA) run along the ring as curved mono text. In RTL the ring decoration mirrors, but the face and the Latin text do not.
Tick-ruler hairlines: every major rule (stats strip, robotic points, BMI panel, footer, treatment meta strip) carries a row of 1px ticks, so dividers read as a measuring scale instead of boxes.

BMI calculator as an instrument: dark panel, mono inputs, a large teal read-out and a 15-45 ruler with the 25/30/35 guideline thresholds and a glowing marker. The scale mirrors in RTL and the original logic, including Arabic-Indic digits and the Arabic decimal separator, is kept (tested with ١٧٢ / ٩٨٫٥).

Sticky mono rail: each section has a '01 / 06' index and name in a narrow start column that sticks while content scrolls; the FAQ heading sticks beside its 15 questions. It collapses to an inline label under 68rem.

Treatments as a typographic index: five full-width rows with mono number, large serif name, summary and a circular arrow that mirrors in RTL; the risk note follows directly as a full-contrast bordered callout, not small print.
Journey as an instrument path: one fine sine curve through four teal nodes with large serif counters 01-04, flipped for RTL and turned into a vertical line on mobile.

FAQ without boxes: native details in three groups, mono counters 01-15, plus/minus on the inline-end, 17-18px answers on a 48rem measure, and a dashed-rule Sources list per answer; details expand in print.

Four abstract line glyphs for the robotic points (stereo lens, wristed joint with angle arc, small marks against a long dashed line, four nodes on a path) and an abstract access figure on the treatment page (entry points on an arc converging on a crosshair); nothing depicts a robot or anatomy.

Footer colophon with the name at display size, then phone in mono with the Faisal disclosure and 997 note at normal contrast. The Faisal line also sits directly under the phone number in the hero and the closing call.
Contact stays calm and constant: teal WhatsApp pill in the hero, a floating WhatsApp pill on desktop, and a 2-button bottom bar on mobile with reserved body padding and scroll-padding.
design:b-precision-dark.innerPagesPlan:
treatment.html shows the inner-page template: a compact dark page hero (mono breadcrumb, large serif h1, summary as lead, one abstract line figure, tick-ruled meta strip with the review line), then a paper reading area of hairline-separated rows with a sticky mono index (01 / 03) and 18-21px text, a dark contact box (phone in mono, Faisal note, WhatsApp button), the disclaimer and review line, and a compact index of the other treatments.

- **About:** same page hero with the small circular portrait and credentials; biography in the reading rows; education, fellowship and certification as the ruled facts list; past KFSHRC experience as a plain dated text row, never a logo.
- **Treatments index:** the homepage typographic list at full size, robotic first, followed by the risk callout.
- **Other treatment pages:** same template, each with its own small abstract figure; the bariatric page adds its ASMBS source in the Sources style used in the FAQ.
- **Journey:** the instrument-path steps expanded vertically, one row per step with large counters, closing with the contact box.
- **Second opinion:** the closing-call composition as the hero, then numbered rows; wording stays question-only, with no request for reports.
- **Resources / Learn / Links:** ruled link lists with mono source labels and external-link arrows.
- **Privacy:** plain reading rows with the sticky index as a table of contents; no decoration beyond the page-hero rule.
- **404 and language redirect:** dark page hero only.

For Astro, the tokens and components map directly onto global.css and Base.astro. The mockup was generated from site.ts and index.astro by a small script, so no copy was retyped.
design:b-precision-dark.pageWeightKB:
Measured as the sum of bytes of every file Chromium actually loaded at 1440px, DPR 1, uncompressed, with zero external requests.

- **index.html (English):** 200.7 KB (HTML 34 + CSS 47 + five fonts 108 + portrait-480.webp 11). About 216 KB on 2x screens, which load the 26 KB portrait-880. With gzip on HTML and CSS it is about 138 KB on the wire.
- **ar.html (Arabic):** 339.4 KB (HTML 43 + CSS 47 + eight fonts 238 + portrait 11). About 355 KB on 2x screens; about 269 KB with gzip.
- **treatment.html:** 165.6 KB.

Baseline for comparison is about 250 KB English and 470 KB Arabic.
design:b-precision-dark.selfCritique:
Checked: 0 axe violations on all three pages, no horizontal overflow at 375, 390 and 1440, BMI tested with Western and Arabic-Indic digits, mobile menu and FAQ open states screenshotted. Not checked: Firefox or Safari, 200%/400% zoom, a keyboard-only pass, and animated states (the helper shoots with reduced motion on).

Weaknesses:
- **Dark is a real risk for this audience.** Roughly 45% of the scroll is near-black. I kept all long reading on paper, but a jury member who wants a calm clinic feel may find the hero and journey more tech than care. The only warmth comes from the portrait, the serif and the paper tone.
- **Newsreader is the static text cut, not the optical-size display cut.** The variable opsz file is 132 KB, so I used weight 300 with tight tracking; the display cut would look finer at 88px.
- **Arabic h1 is very large and heavy** (Markazi 500 at about 138px), which pushes the stats strip below the first desktop viewport on the Arabic page. Markazi sizing was tuned by eye from screenshots only and needs a native reader's review, as does the diacritic clearance on words like بدقّة.
- **The Arabic page still loads four Latin font files** (about 85 KB) for digits, acronyms and citations; subsetting those to digits and capitals would cut most of that.
- **The language-switch word "العربية" on the English page uses a system font**, to avoid downloading 43 KB of Plex Arabic for one word. In the screenshots it renders in DejaVu; production should ship a tiny subset.
- **A few layout-only labels are new and need owner approval:** FAQ group headings (Before a decision / Life after surgery / Practical matters), "Sourced answers", "Sources", "Risks" and "Menu", with Arabic equivalents. No medical wording was changed.
- **The curved credentials text on the dial is about 10px on desktop.** It is decorative and aria-hidden (the credentials appear as real text elsewhere), but it is small.
- **On mobile the portrait sits below the fold**, under the copy and call to action; only its top edge shows in the first screen.
- **Mixed arrows:** the approved "→ / ←" characters in the journey and about links are kept as text beside the SVG arrows used elsewhere.
- **The paths section has dead space** under the two lists on desktop, beside the taller BMI panel.
- **CSS is 47 KB unminified** (about 10 KB gzipped) and has some per-language overrides that would be tidier as tokens.
- **Inner-page links are "#" placeholders**, except the home/Arabic switch and the Robotic Surgery row.

With more time I would subset the fonts, test the optical-size display cut, add a per-treatment figure set, tune the Arabic hero scale with a native typographer, and run the cross-browser, zoom and keyboard passes.

design:c-arabic-first.name: C — Arabic-first modern Saudi ("Khatim")
design:c-arabic-first.concept: The Arabic page was designed first and the English derived from it. One bilingual geometric display family (Alexandria, set light) carries headlines in both scripts over IBM Plex Sans Arabic for reading, so neither language looks like a translation of the other. The palette is a deep desaturated green on warm paper with a brass hairline accent, and there is exactly one dark band (the robotic section). A single motif — the eight-pointed star made of two squares, drawn as fine concentric lines — appears behind the portrait, in the monogram and quote mark, and in the closing contact panel. Structure comes from hairlines, large light numerals and a recurring "leaf" corner (portrait, BMI panel, featured treatment, contact panel) instead of cards and shadows.
design:c-arabic-first.typography: Display: Alexandria variable (Arabic + Latin subsets, weight 200–500, mostly 300) for h1/h2, numerals, stats, phone number and footer colophon. Text and UI: IBM Plex Sans Arabic 400/600 (its Arabic subset for Arabic, its Latin subset for English). Arabic is the default scale: body 19px at line-height 1.85, h1 up to 98px at line-height 1.28, no tracking, no italics, no uppercase (global :lang(ar) reset), eyebrows by weight, colour and a short brass rule. English overrides: body 17px/1.65, h1 up to 74px with -0.035em tracking, uppercase tracked eyebrows. All sizes are rem + vw clamps with max no more than 2.5x min. Western digits throughout; phone numbers, FACS and ASMBS/IFSO/BMI tokens are isolated LTR.
design:c-arabic-first.palette: Paper #FBFAF6, sand #F2EDE2, ink #0B1F1B, body #2C3B37, muted #54625D, green accent #0E5E49, deep green band #0A2E27, brass #B8924A (decorative lines only, never text on light), on dark: #F4F1E8 text, mint #A8DEC9 accent, light brass #DFC591. axe-core reports 0 violations (WCAG 2.0–2.2 A/AA plus best-practice rules) on all three pages at 1440 and 390 wide, with every FAQ expanded.
signatureMoves: Arabic headline in light Alexandria at about 98px, larger than the English one, with the second line in green — the contemporary Saudi brand look in place of the classical Amiri

One motif only: concentric eight-pointed-star linework in brass, cropped by the page edge behind the portrait and by the closing contact panel; the same star frames the monogram ('ع ح' in Arabic, 'AH' in English)
Leaf-corner shape (one or two large logical-property radii) on the portrait, BMI panel, featured treatment and contact panel; it mirrors automatically in RTL while the face is never flipped
Treatments as one featured deep-green Robotic Surgery card beside a ruled, numbered list of the other four, followed by the risk note at full body size
Journey as four steps on a single hairline with brass diamond nodes and very large light numerals 01–04; it runs right-to-left in Arabic and becomes a vertical line on mobile
BMI calculator with a four-band scale and marker that reads low-to-high from the right in Arabic; original logic kept, including Arabic-Indic digit and ٫ separator input
FAQ as 15 numbered native details rows with a sticky side heading carrying the 'Medically reviewed' line; sources listed under each answer
Faisal AI-assistant disclosure sits directly under the phone number in the hero, the closing panel, the treatment contact box and the footer
Footer colophon: the doctor's name set across the page in weight 200 green, above three plain columns
Abstract line drawing for robotic surgery (a magnified field with three fine instrument paths meeting at a point) — no machine, vendor shape or people
design:c-arabic-first.innerPagesPlan:
treatment.html shows the inner-page pattern: breadcrumb with brass diamond separators, a page hero (large light h1, summary as lead, the abstract drawing in the end columns), then numbered ruled rows with the heading in the start columns and the copy at lead size in the end columns, a leaf-cornered deep-green contact panel (phone, WhatsApp button, Faisal note), the disclaimer and reviewed line, and a ruled list of the other treatments with the risk note.

- About: same page hero with the small leaf portrait; the story as a reading column with a sticky side label; credentials as the ruled definition list already used on the homepage; past KFSHRC experience as a plain dated row, no logos.
- Treatments index: the homepage featured-card-plus-ruled-list block at full size, risk note beneath.
- Each treatment: the numbered rows (What it is / Who it may suit / What to expect); the bariatric page adds its source line in the sources style used under FAQ answers.
- Journey: the homepage steps component expanded vertically, one large numeral per stage on a continuous hairline.
- Second opinion: page hero plus the closing contact panel promoted to the top, with the "question only" wording.
- Resources / Learn: ruled link lists using the treatment-row component, external sources in the FAQ source style.
- Privacy: single reading column (about 65 characters) with numbered ruled rows; approved text untouched.
- Header, footer, floating WhatsApp pill (desktop) and two-button contact bar (mobile) are shared by every page.
design:c-arabic-first.pageWeightKB: Measured as the sum of files Chromium actually requested at 1440px, 1x DPR, uncompressed bytes on disk: index.html (English) 175 KB; ar.html (Arabic) 270 KB; treatment.html 144 KB. On a 2x screen the hero loads the 880px portrait as well, adding about 29 KB (roughly 204 KB English, 299 KB Arabic). Current site for comparison: about 250 KB English, 470 KB Arabic. Breakdown: HTML 30 KB (en) / 39 KB (ar), CSS 37 KB, portrait WebP 11 KB (480w) + 29 KB (880w), fonts 101 KB on English (Alexandria Latin 30, Alexandria Arabic 31 for the language switch, Plex Latin 400 19 + 600 21) and 190 KB on Arabic (adds Plex Arabic 400 43 + 600 46). No external requests.
design:c-arabic-first.selfCritique:
- Typeface risk: Alexandria's Latin is a Montserrat-family geometric. The English page is clean but less distinctive than the Arabic one, and it gives up the serif warmth of the current site. A jury that prefers editorial serif may find the English a little corporate.
- The English page downloads the 31 KB Alexandria Arabic file only to draw the word "العربية" in the language switch. A tiny subset or a system-font fallback would remove it.
- The eight-pointed star is restrained here, but it is still the most familiar Islamic geometric figure. A Najdi-specific motif would be more original and I did not explore one.
- The abstract robotic drawing is used three times (dark band, featured card, treatment hero) and is fairly plain. I did not draw per-treatment icons or the numbered anatomical diagrams the research suggested.
- The Arabic monogram "ع ح" is my invention (a single ع read like the digit ٤). It needs the owner's approval, as do the Arabic accessible names I wrote for the nav, contact region and breadcrumb.
- I added the approved Faisal sentence under the phone number in the hero and closing panel, and a caption under the portrait with the name and credentials. These are placement changes, not new wording, but the owner should confirm them.
- I replaced the literal arrow characters in "Your journey in detail →" and "Read the full story →" with a mirrored SVG arrow, because the Latin font subsets do not contain arrows.
- Checked: axe at two widths, no horizontal overflow at 375/390/1440, BMI with Arabic-Indic input, FAQ open state. Not checked: Firefox or Safari rendering, 200% zoom, a manual keyboard pass, real-device Arabic rendering. The screenshot helper forces reduced motion, so the hero entrance and FAQ open animation were never seen running.
- On mobile the header is two rows with a horizontally scrolling nav that has no scroll affordance, and the hero portrait is small. On desktop the sticky header hides section tops in the segment screenshots.
- The footer colophon does not span the full width in Arabic, the journey heading leaves the right two-thirds of its row empty in English, and the empty BMI result area reserves a lot of blank height.
- The mockup is produced by a generator script that reads the real copy from the repo, so wording is verbatim, but nothing has been ported to Astro components. Only "Home", the language switch and Robotic Surgery link anywhere; other links are "#".
- With more time: test a serif Latin companion for English display, draw a per-treatment icon set, add a print stylesheet that expands the FAQ, add metric-matched fallback fonts to prevent layout shift, and build Arabic versions of the inner pages.

design:d-human-warmth.name: d-human-warmth — "A conversation, then a path"
design:d-human-warmth.concept: The site is built around the two things a worried patient actually wants: someone who will listen, and a clear idea of what happens next. Every panel uses one recurring form, the "leaf" (a soft rounded panel with one tighter corner, like a speech bubble), and one recurring line, a dotted winding path that appears in the brand mark, the robotic section, the treatment art and finally as the real four-station patient journey. The portrait sits in a large leaf-shaped frame on warm sand with a name card, and the doctor's own quote gets a full section directly under the hero with a small second portrait. I moved "Not every patient needs surgery" and the BMI check ahead of the robotics section so the page leads with the patient's situation; all approved wording, all 15 FAQs with their sources, the risk note, the Faisal disclosure and the 997 note are reproduced verbatim from the repo. Arabic is composed separately (Markazi Text display at larger sizes, IBM Plex Sans Arabic body, no tracking or italics, journey and BMI scale running right to left).
design:d-human-warmth.typography: English: Fraunces variable with the SOFT axis at 100 for display (weight ~380, -0.022em tracking), Fraunces italic for the single emphasised phrase per heading and the quote, Figtree variable for body and UI (17px, line-height 1.62). Arabic: Markazi Text variable (weight 500) for h1/h2, quote and card titles, set about 1.3 to 1.5x the Latin sizes with line-height 1.12 to 1.4; IBM Plex Sans Arabic 400/600 for body (18px, line-height 1.85) and h3. Latin tokens inside Arabic (FACS, 15+, phone number, credentials) fall through to Fraunces/Figtree via unicode-range and are isolated with bdi/dir=ltr. A global :lang(ar) reset removes letter-spacing, uppercase and italics. All fluid sizes are rem + vw with max no more than 2.5x min. Amiri, Inter and Newsreader are no longer used.
design:d-human-warmth.palette: Warm paper #fbf6ee, card #fffdf8, sand #f3e9da (hero, alternating bands, footer), sage #dfe6d6 / #c7d4bd (soft panels, portrait backdrop), deep pine #1f3b34 (the grounded accent: buttons, featured treatment card, closing call), clay #a14524 (eyebrows, italic emphasis, numerals, path line) with clay wash #f7e3d5 (risk note, "with surgery" card). Text ink #2a2520, body #4a413a, muted #675c52. axe-core reports 0 violations, including colour contrast, on all three pages at 1440 and 375 with every FAQ open.
signatureMoves: The 'leaf' panel: one radius system where every card, the portrait frame, the stats tray, FAQ rows and the brand mark share a soft shape with one tight corner (speech-bubble cue); built with logical radii so it mirrors in RTL

The patient journey as a real visual path: a dotted winding line through four numbered stations on desktop (flipped for Arabic so it runs right to left), collapsing to a vertical dotted trail on mobile

Portrait and voice given presence: large leaf-framed portrait with sage backdrop, clay outline and a name/credentials card; then a full-width quote section in Fraunces italic (Markazi in Arabic) signed with a small round portrait

Patient-first ordering: 'Not every patient needs surgery' with two equal path cards (sage = without surgery, clay wash = with surgery) beside a sticky BMI card that now shows a soft colour scale with a marker at the 25/30/35 guideline thresholds; accepts Arabic-Indic digits and the scale mirrors in RTL
Honest risk note given body-size type in its own clay-wash leaf directly under the treatments, not as fine print

Contact stays calm and constant: one pine WhatsApp button per screen, the Faisal AI-assistant line directly under every phone number, a 60px icon button on desktop and a two-button bottom bar on mobile with reserved padding
Full-width name colophon footer in display type (Arabic name set in Markazi at up to ~8.5rem)
FAQ as numbered native details rows with a plus that rotates to a cross, sources listed inside each answer, height animation only where interpolate-size is supported
design:d-human-warmth.innerPagesPlan: treatment.html shows the inner-page template: sand page-hero with rounded bottom, breadcrumb, large h1, summary as lead and the concentric-arc/path art; body as numbered leaf steps (01 What it is, 02 Who it may suit, 03 What to expect) beside a sticky pine contact card (phone, Faisal line, WhatsApp) and a clay-wash note holding the general-information disclaimer and the medically-reviewed line; then the other treatments as a hairline list plus the risk note. About: same page-hero with the portrait in the leaf frame (the one large use on that page), the facts dl card from the homepage extended to the full credentials list, past experience (including KFSHRC, clearly past tense) as a vertical dotted path timeline. Treatments index: the featured pine card plus four leaf cards, as on the homepage, with the risk note. Journey: the path component expanded, one leaf step per stage with the vertical dotted trail down the page on all breakpoints. Second opinion: page-hero plus the pine closing-call panel as the main block, with "question only, no reports" stated in a clay-wash note. Resources and Learn: hairline link lists (the more-list component) grouped under h2s with source names as plain text. Privacy: single reading column (about 65ch) of the approved text with leaf-shaped summary notes for 'no analytics, no cookies, no third-party requests'. Header, footer, contact bar and the :lang(ar) rules are shared unchanged.
design:d-human-warmth.pageWeightKB: Measured as uncompressed bytes of every file the browser actually requested (HTML + CSS + fonts + images) at 1x: index.html 213.8 KB (HTML 35.7, CSS 40.8, Fraunces soft 62.4, Fraunces italic 45.7, Figtree 20.2, portraits 14.3); ar.html 304.5 KB (HTML 44.4, CSS 40.8, Plex Arabic 400+600 88.5, Markazi 41.3, Fraunces soft 62.4, Figtree 20.2, portraits 14.3); treatment.html 130.3 KB. On 2x screens the 880px portrait replaces the 520px one, adding about 16 KB. HTML and CSS are unminified and uncompressed, so real transfer would be lower. Baseline was about 250 KB (EN) and 470 KB (AR).
design:d-human-warmth.selfCritique: Weaknesses I can see. (1) Rounded cards are the direction, but it is the most card-heavy of the likely entries; the treatments grid (one feature + four equal cards with small icons) is the closest thing to a template pattern and the four abstract icons are generic rather than a bespoke illustration system. (2) The portrait frame is a CSS elliptical-radius shape; its lower inline-end curve and the offset sage backdrop look slightly improvised compared with a hand-drawn SVG mask, and on mobile the portrait sits above the h1, pushing the headline to about 60% down the first screen. (3) Fraunces is shipped with the SOFT axis but without optical sizing, so large headings use the text cut; they read friendly but a little heavier than a true display cut. (4) The English page loads two Fraunces files (108 KB) mainly so the quote and one phrase per heading can be italic. (5) The Arabic page still loads the 62 KB Fraunces file only for Latin tokens and numerals (FACS, 15+, step numbers); a subset would cut it to a few KB. (6) Arabic h3s are Plex while some card titles are Markazi, a small inconsistency; Markazi Text sizes were tuned by eye from screenshots only, and I did not test Readex Pro or other candidates. (7) The desktop journey line is a stretched SVG, so its curve flattens on very wide screens and the stations are centre-aligned text, which is less editorial than the rest. (8) On the desktop the floating contact button is icon-only (visually hidden label) to stop it covering content. (9) I reordered sections (paths and BMI before robotics) and added the Faisal line under the hero and closing phone links plus a BMI scale graphic with 25/30/35 ticks; these use only approved wording and the calculator's own thresholds, but the owner should confirm the reorder. (10) Not verified: Firefox/Safari rendering, 200% and 400% zoom, forced-colours mode, keyboard walk-through by hand (axe only), and the scroll-driven reveal/hero entrance animations (screenshots run with reduced motion). In-page links other than the language switch and Robotic Surgery point to anchors or '#' because this is a mockup. With more time: draw the portrait mask and treatment illustrations as one SVG system, subset fonts, try text-first hero on mobile, and build the Arabic treatment page.

strengths: Most coherent typographic system of the four: Newsreader optical-size display at about 92px against 12px tracked labels gives real scale contrast, and the hairline grid holds from hero to colophon
The portrait as a square plate with crop marks and a caption on a hairline is a restrained idea that reads as designed, and it recurs convincingly on the second-opinion block
Treatments as an oversized typographic index (number, 50px serif name, summary, arrow) is the single best section in the whole panel
Journey with large accent numerals hanging from one dotted hairline is elegant and needs no decoration
Clear page rhythm: paper, one ink band, paper, sand, paper, sand, framed closing block, full-width name colophon
The dark robotic band with faint concentric arcs is the right amount of atmosphere and stays calm
Mobile holds up: headline and WhatsApp button in the first screen, stats strip reflows cleanly into rows
Reads as hand-set print rather than a template; no cards, shadows or icon clutter
weaknesses: The hero composition is the baseline's (text left, portrait right, three-cell strip) refined rather than reinvented, so it is the least surprising entry
Losing the baseline's italic second line removes some charm; the roman green line is slightly flat
Arabic is weaker than English: the Markazi headline at this size looks heavy and plain beside the fine Newsreader cut, so the two languages do not feel like equals
Long stretches of beige-on-beige in the lower half (about, FAQ) with little visual event; the page is beautiful but low on memorability after the treatments index
The numbered section rule repeats '01' twice in close succession in the robotic band (section 01, then point 01), which reads as a stutter
The BMI panel is the plainest element: boxed inputs and a flat sand rectangle, less considered than the rest
defects: Mobile navigation wraps to two rows of plain links (English and Arabic) instead of a designed menu, costing about 100px of the first screen
Desktop floating WhatsApp pill overlaps content at the bottom corner: it covers the right stat cell border on the hero and the last treatment row arrow, and sits on the robotic band artwork

Winner on aesthetic craft: A (quiet luxury editorial), 84. B is second at 80, C 70, D 66.

A wins because it is the only entry where typography alone carries the page. The optical-size serif, the hairline grid, the crop-marked portrait plate, the oversized treatments index and the name colophon form one disciplined system that looks hand-set and suits a consultant surgeon. B has the single most memorable image (the portrait dial) and the best instrument details, but its dark-teal-mono-HUD vocabulary is the most recognisably generic "AI dark tech" look. It is also tonally wrong for worried patients, and it had the most overlap defects in the screenshots. C has the best Arabic page but a corporate, characterless English one and a broken mobile hero. D is warm but is a card-and-pastel wellness template.

Is A genuinely better than the live site? Yes, but by a moderate margin. The baseline is already a clean, tasteful serif-on-paper design with an arch portrait and an italic accent line, and A is an evolution of the same idea rather than a new one. A is clearly better in these places:
- display type quality and scale contrast
- the treatments index, replacing a plain list
- the journey numerals
- the framed closing block and the name colophon
- the Faisal disclosure placed under every phone number
- a properly composed dark band
- a lighter Arabic page

A is not yet better in these places, and should not ship until they are fixed:
- the mobile navigation (two wrapped rows, where the baseline has a single row)
- the Arabic headline, which is heavier and plainer than the baseline's Amiri and needs a native reader's judgement
- the lost italic accent
- the floating WhatsApp pill overlapping content on desktop

With those fixed and the grafts from B (mobile menu, instrument BMI scale, section rail, per-treatment line figures) and C (Arabic display tuning, brass hairline), A would be a clear step up. As it stands it is a refinement, not a transformation.

judge:patient-trust-objectives.verdict:
Winner on the patient-trust lens: A (Quiet luxury), ahead of C (Arabic-first), D (Human warmth) and B (Precision dark).

All four pass the rule check. I searched the text of every index, Arabic and treatment page: no superlatives or guarantees (the only "guaranteed" is the approved "cannot be guaranteed"; "best approach for you" on the treatment page is existing approved copy), no booking wording, no vendor names, KFSHRC only as past experience, no request for medical records, 15 FAQs with source links in both languages, the Faisal AI disclosure and the 997 note present, and no external requests. The differences are therefore about tone and usability, not compliance.

A wins because it looks like what the patient is being asked to trust: a senior consultant. The first screen gives the name, role, honest claim, WhatsApp button, phone and Faisal disclosure in both languages, and the risk paragraph is at full size. C has the best Arabic and the most Saudi-appropriate palette, but its English is corporate, its WhatsApp icon is generic and its mobile hero shrinks the face. D is the kindest to an anxious patient and has the best section order, but it reads as a wellness clinic and its quote-with-avatar block looks like a testimonial. B is impressive but cold; the crosshair ring around the face and the neon-on-black palette work against trust.

Is A better than the live site? Yes, but as a refinement, not a transformation. The live design is already clean, compliant and dignified. A's real gains are: the Faisal disclosure and credentials visible on the first screen, a recognisable WhatsApp button as the only filled colour, a far clearer treatments index with the risk note at body size, numbered structure through a long page, and an Arabic page about 170 KB lighter. Its losses are a little warmth (no italic line, a squarer portrait) and 30-45 KB on the English page.

A should only replace the live site after its defects are fixed (floating pill overlap, mobile nav, an axe run) and after it takes D's patient-first order, risk callout and BMI scale, and a test of C's Arabic display face. Without those, the improvement over the baseline is too small to justify the change.

judge:engineering-a11y-rtl.verdict:
On the engineering, accessibility and RTL lens, C (Arabic-first) wins, with B a close second and A third only because of measurable but quickly fixable failures.

I ran axe-core on index, ar and treatment for all four at 1440 and 390 with every FAQ open, tabbed through 137-138 stops per page at desktop and 375px, checked reflow at 375 and 320, tested reduced motion and no-JavaScript, measured loaded bytes, and did my own contrast sweep. Not checked: Firefox, Safari, real devices, 200% zoom, forced-colours mode, and the animations in motion.

| | axe violations | 320px reflow | English / Arabic weight | Per-language CSS rules |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C | 0 | 1px overflow in bottom bar | 175 / 270 KB | 15 |
| B | 0 | clean | 196 / 331 KB | 49 |
| A | 2 moderate (best-practice) | fails, page scrolls sideways | 279 / 286 KB | 43 |
| D | 0 | Call button clipped 37px | 214 / 305 KB | 37 |

- **Why C:** it is the lightest, has the simplest font stack (6 files), no text under 13px, and needs the fewest Arabic overrides because Arabic is the default. That last point matters most for extending to 10 inner page types without bloat.
- **Why not B:** it has the best reflow and the only real mobile menu, but the most bespoke CSS and the heaviest Arabic page.
- **Why not A:** it has the cleanest code and would port most easily, but it fails 320px reflow, is not at zero axe violations, and its English page is heavier than the live site.
- **Why not D:** it is the most component-heavy and has a clipped phone number at 320px.

**Is the winner genuinely better than the live site? Yes, on what I measured, but it is an evolution.** Arabic weight falls from about 470 KB to 270 KB and English from about 250 KB to 175 KB. The Faisal disclosure now sits under the phone number in the hero, which the live hero lacks. The risk note is at full body size, and the BMI tool gains a scale. The live site already has a clean hero and the same scrolling mobile nav flaw, so the gain is real but not dramatic.

C should only ship after these fixes: replace the scrolling mobile nav with B's menu, fix the 320px bar, drop the 31 KB Arabic font from the English page, and get owner approval for the Arabic monogram. Whether English should lose its serif is a design call outside my lens.
